"List of New York Giants head coaches") [Tom Coughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Coughlin "Tom Coughlin"). The Giants finished the regular season 10–6 and in second place in the NFC East, improving upon their 8–8 record in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_New_York_Giants_season "2006 New York Giants season") in which they finished third in their division.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-1) They qualified for the playoffs as a [wild-card team as the #5 seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_NFL_playoffs "2007–08 NFL playoffs"), and beat the #4 seed [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers_season "2007 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season") 24–14. Next, they defeated the top-seeded [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2007 Dallas Cowboys season") 21–17 and the #2 seed [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season "2007 Green Bay Packers season") 23–20 (both of whom they had lost to in their first two games of the season by ten points or more) to become the [National Football Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_Conference "National Football Conference") (NFC) representative in [Super Bowl XLII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII "Super Bowl XLII").[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-2) There, they defeated the heavily favored and previously undefeated [18–0 New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_England_Patriots_season "2007 New England Patriots season") 17–14 and spoiled their [perfect season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfect_season "Perfect season"), aided by the famous [Manning to Tyree Helmet Catch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmet_Catch "Helmet Catch").[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-5) The 2007 New York Giants became the 9th wild card team in NFL history to reach the Super Bowl and the 5th wild card team to win the Super Bowl, and the very first [NFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_Conference "National Football Conference") wild card to accomplish the feat. They were the third team in history to win three road playoff games en route to a Super Bowl and set a league record for most consecutive road wins in a single season (11), though the Super Bowl is played on a neutral field rather than an opponent's stadium.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-6) It was the 7th league championship season for the New York Giants and their first since they won [Super Bowl XXV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXV "Super Bowl XXV") in [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_NFL_season "1990 NFL season"). This season would also mark the end of defensive end [Michael Strahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Strahan "Michael Strahan")'s NFL career as he retired following the Giants' Super Bowl victory. This was the first season since [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_New_York_Giants_season "1996 New York Giants season") that [Tiki Barber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiki_Barber "Tiki Barber") was not on the opening-day roster. 2007 marked the third consecutive season that the Giants made the playoffs, which was only the second time that had happened since the AFL–NFL merger in 1970. Tom Coughlin joined [Bill Parcells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Parcells "Bill Parcells"), [Steve Owen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Owen_/(American_football/) "Steve Owen (American football)"), and [Allie Sherman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allie_Sherman "Allie Sherman") as the only head coaches in the history of the team to lead the Giants to the postseason three consecutive years. The Giants season is widely regarded as one of the greatest [cinderella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinderella_/(sports/) "Cinderella (sports)") stories in professional sports history, as not only did they beat one of the greatest teams of all time in the undefeated Patriots, they did so as a wild-card team that had to win three playoff games on the road to get to [Super Bowl XLII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII "Super Bowl XLII"), which gave them the nickname of "The Road Warriors",[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-10) and after looking very mediocre at times during the regular season.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-13)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-14)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-15)[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-16) In fact, based on regular-season performance, the 2007 New York Giants were the worst team to ever reach a Super Bowl,[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-z516-17) a curiosity later surpassed when the [2011 New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_New_York_Giants_season "2011 New York Giants season") won [Super Bowl XLVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLVI "Super Bowl XLVI") to become the first team with a negative point differential to win a Super Bowl.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-18) NFL Films named the 2007 Giants as the 53rd greatest team of all time in their countdown of the top 100 teams in football history.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-19) After their poor finish to the [2006 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_New_York_Giants_season "2006 New York Giants season"), where the Giants lost 7 of their last 9 games after a 6–2 start (albeit achieving a playoff berth in the last week of the season), expectations for the Giants were generally low. Many pundits began to consider [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") as a potential draft bust, especially when considering fellow 2004 draft pick [Ben Roethlisberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Roethlisberger "Ben Roethlisberger")'s Super Bowl run in 2005 and [Philip Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Rivers "Philip Rivers") leading his team, the Chargers, to a 14–2 regular season in 2006; making matters worse, older brother [Peyton Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peyton_Manning "Peyton Manning"), who Eli was often compared unfavorably to, had led the Colts to the Super Bowl victory that same year and won the MVP of the game. At the same time, head coach [Tom Coughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Coughlin "Tom Coughlin") came under intense criticism due to his fiery coaching style and strict team rules, and many (including fans) believed that he deserved to be fired after the team's collapse in the second half of the season. In particular, they noted the team's lack of discipline and unity down the stretch and considered these actions a reflection of Coughlin's coaching. Finally [Tiki Barber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiki_Barber "Tiki Barber"), the Giants's all-time leading rusher and the catalyst for much of their success the previous two seasons, retired at just 31 years of age to enter a broadcasting career. The Giants decided to give Tom Coughlin one more chance heading into the 2007 season, giving him a one-year contract extension. This essentially indicated that he needed to get the Giants into the postseason in order to receive a long-term contract extension. After his family demonstrated concern over his on-field persona and his apparent anger towards his players, Coughlin decided to undergo a personality change heading into the season. While his strict team rules (most notoriously, his five-minute early rule for a team meeting) remained in place, he became less angry and more encouraging towards his players, and the players took note of his change. Coughlin also set up a leadership committee with [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") and other team captains in order to relate to his players better. The Giants also entered the season with two new coordinators. Coughlin promoted quarterbacks coach [Kevin Gilbride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Gilbride "Kevin Gilbride") to offensive coordinator, a position he would hold until his retirement after the 2013 season. He also fired defensive coordinator [Tim Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Lewis "Tim Lewis") and replaced him with [Steve Spagnuolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Spagnuolo "Steve Spagnuolo"), who would have a crucial impact on the Giants's 4-3 defense. Defensive end [Michael Strahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Strahan "Michael Strahan") held out for the entirety of training camp. Having previously been disillusioned with Tom Coughlin's coaching methods, he spent the offseason debating whether or not he would come back for the season, and decided that since he had already played for 14 seasons, he wouldn't have needed the training camp anyway. He eventually returned to the team mere weeks before the season started. Despite his training camp holdout and a hefty fine for not attending the camp, he was still elected as a team captain. Expectations, however, were still low as few predicted that the Giants would make the playoffs. Perception grew worse as Tiki Barber, now an analyst for NBC, began attacking his former team, particularly Tom Coughlin and especially Eli Manning. Barber attacked Manning not only as a non-productive quarterback, but declared that his leadership skills were "almost comical." When asked about Barber's comments, Manning noted that he didn't have to take the comments seriously, considering that Barber announced his intentions to leave the team in the middle of the previous season. ### Week 1: at Dallas Cowboys \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=12 "Edit section: Week 1: at Dallas Cowboys")\] The Giants opened up their 2007 campaign with a 45–35 loss to the Dallas Cowboys at Texas Stadium. For the second straight year, the Giants left Dallas with injuries to key starters including defensive end [Osi Umenyiora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osi_Umenyiora "Osi Umenyiora"), running back [Brandon Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jacobs "Brandon Jacobs"), and quarterback [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning"). Before suffering a separated shoulder in the fourth quarter, Manning put on a stellar performance, completing 28 of 41 passes, for 312 yards, 4 touchdowns and just 1 interception. However, a horrid defensive performance overshadowed his play. The Giants got off to a fast start as Manning hit [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress") on a 60-yard touchdown pass off play action to open up the scoring. Burress and Manning would connect for 3 touchdowns on the night. After a Dallas took a 17–6 lead late in the half, Manning led the Giants on another drive, capped off to his second strike to Burress. Burress on the night caught 9 passes for 144 receiving yards. The Giants closed to within one at half's end following a [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes") field goal after a Dallas fumble. Romo hit [Terrell Owens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrell_Owens "Terrell Owens") on a 22-yard pass to give Dallas an 8-point lead. After the Giants cut the lead to five on another Tynes field goal, Dallas increased the margin to 12 as Romo capped off a quick four play drive with a 9-yard rush. The Cowboys appeared to put the game away with yet another Romo touchdown, once again finding Terrell Owens on a wide open catch and run, upping margin to 38–22. Eli and the Giants responded with two straight scoring drives. One finished with a dumpoff touchdown pass from Manning to reserve running back [Derrick Ward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Ward "Derrick Ward") and the other with Burress' third touchdown, cutting the Dallas lead to three. On a crucial 3rd and 7 late in the game, Romo hit backup wideout [Sam Hurd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Hurd "Sam Hurd") for a 51-yard touchdown. With Manning injuring his shoulder, backup [Jared Lorenzen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jared_Lorenzen "Jared Lorenzen") finished the game for the Giants at quarterback late in the fourth quarter. [Amani Toomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amani_Toomer "Amani Toomer") in his return from a knee injury, notched 9 catches for 91 yards while Burress gained 144. [Justin Tuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Tuck "Justin Tuck") and [Gibril Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibril_Wilson "Gibril Wilson") recorded the Giants' only sack and interception of the night respectively in the 45–35 loss as the Giants began the season at 0–1. It would be the only road loss for the Giants in the season.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-2007pfr-24) ### Week 2: vs. Green Bay Packers \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=13 "Edit section: Week 2: vs. Green Bay Packers")\] [![Image 9](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/GBNYShotgun.jpg/250px-GBNYShotgun.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GBNYShotgun.jpg) The Giants playing defense against the Packers The Giants played their Week 2 home opener against the [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers"). After both teams missed a field goal to open the game, Green Bay got on the board first with a 6-yard run by rookie DeShawn Wynn. The Giants responded with a 26-yard scoring strike by Eli Manning to Plaxico Burress. The Giants got a Lawrence Tynes field goal and a 10–7 half time lead. In the second half, the Packers drove 51 yards to start the second half. Favre capped off the scoring drive with a 2-yard pass to Bubba Franks for a 14–10 lead the Packers would not relinquish. The Giants responded with another drive but once again, an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, this one on Amani Toomer, hurt the Giants. Tynes kicked a second field goal, pulling the Giants to within one.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-September16th-25) The Packers went on to score 21 unanswered points.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-September16th-25) With the loss, the Giants would fall to 0–2 for the first time since 1996. Also, within the two games they played, the Giants gave up a total of 80 points. ### Week 3: at Washington Redskins \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=14 "Edit section: Week 3: at Washington Redskins")\] In the first quarter, New York got the first score as kicker [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes") hit a 34-yard field goal. The Redskins took the lead with running back [Clinton Portis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_Portis "Clinton Portis") getting a 1-yard TD run. In the second quarter, Redskins quarterback [Jason Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Campbell "Jason Campbell") threw an 8-yard touchdown pass to tight end [Chris Cooley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Cooley_/(American_football/) "Chris Cooley (American football)"), while kicker [Shaun Suisham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Suisham "Shaun Suisham") ended the half with a 47-yard field goal that gave Washington a 17–3 lead.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-26) [![Image 10](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/Redskins_vs_Giants_line_of_scrimmage_throwbacks.jpg/250px-Redskins_vs_Giants_line_of_scrimmage_throwbacks.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Redskins_vs_Giants_line_of_scrimmage_throwbacks.jpg) The Giants on defense against the Redskins With the Giants staring at a 14-point deficit, and an 0–2 start to their season, the Giants came out strong to start the second half. In the third quarter, quarterback [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") finally got the Giants offense turned around and running back [Reuben Droughns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuben_Droughns "Reuben Droughns") would score on a 1-yard touchdown run to cut the lead in half. In the fourth quarter, Droughns rushed again for a 1-yard touchdown, while Manning completed a 33-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress"), giving the Giants a startling 24–17 lead against the home team. In the game's final moments, Washington found first and goal at the Giants 1-yard line. New York's defense then proceeded to make a goal-line stand as they stopped running back [Ladell Betts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladell_Betts "Ladell Betts") from getting into the end zone on 4th down during the final seconds of the game. This goal line stand was known as the initial catalyst of the Giants' Super Bowl season. With the win, the Giants improved to 1–2.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-2007pfr-24) ### Week 4: vs. Philadelphia Eagles \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=15 "Edit section: Week 4: vs. Philadelphia Eagles")\] Coming off their divisional road win over the Redskins, the Giants went home for a Sunday night divisional duel with the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles"). New York's defense held the Eagles to no first half points, while in the second quarter, New York got on the board first with quarterback [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") completing a 9-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress") for the only score of the half. In the third quarter, the Giants increased its lead with kicker [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes") getting a 29-yard field goal, along with linebacker [Kawika Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawika_Mitchell "Kawika Mitchell") recovering a fumble, getting up, and returning the fumble 17-yards for a touchdown. In the fourth quarter, the Eagles would get their only points of the game with kicker [David Akers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Akers "David Akers") making a 53-yard field goal. On the night, New York's defense sacked quarterback [Donovan McNabb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donovan_McNabb "Donovan McNabb") 12 times (tying an NFL record), with half of those sacks coming from defensive end [Osi Umenyiora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osi_Umenyiora "Osi Umenyiora"). Also, defensive end [Michael Strahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Strahan "Michael Strahan") had one sack in the game to surpass [Lawrence Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Taylor "Lawrence Taylor") as the Giants' all-time sack leader (Taylor was present at the game). With the victory, New York improved to 2–2.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-2007pfr-24) ### Week 5: vs. New York Jets \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=16 "Edit section: Week 5: vs. New York Jets")\] The Giants clinched their third straight victory with a 35–24 triumph over the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets"). The Giants scored 28 points in the decisive second half to overcome a 10-point deficit. Rookie cornerback [Aaron Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Ross "Aaron Ross") made his presence felt with a crucial interception off of quarterback [Chad Pennington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad_Pennington "Chad Pennington") with the Jets driving and up three in the third then sealed the win with an interception return for a touchdown late in the fourth. The Jets got off to a fast start as returning running back [Brandon Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jacobs "Brandon Jacobs") fumbled and the Jets' [Kerry Rhodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerry_Rhodes "Kerry Rhodes") returned it for a touchdown. The Giants responded with a 9-play, 67-yard drive ending in a touchdown run by [Derrick Ward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Ward "Derrick Ward"). However, the Giants defense, susceptible to third down conversions the first week of the season struggled again today and allowed the Jets to drive 93 yards late in the half for a 14–7 lead. The Jets were 3 for 3 on third down on the drive including some big catches by [Laveranues Coles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laveranues_Coles "Laveranues Coles"). Pennington hit [Brad Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Smith_/(American_football,_born_1983/) "Brad Smith (American football, born 1983)") for a 16-yard touchdown. After a bad interception from [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning"), the Jets added a field goal by [Mike Nugent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Nugent "Mike Nugent") for a 17–7 halftime lead. The Giants fought back, going back to the ground game to start the second half. [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress") added a 25-yard completion from Manning and Jacobs pounded it in for a 19-yard touchdown. The Jets responded as [Leon Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Washington "Leon Washington") ran 98 yards for a touchdown. Big Blue again fought back, driving 68 yards featuring a mix of runs and passes. [Jeremy Shockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Shockey "Jeremy Shockey") notched his first touchdown of the season with a 13-yard catch and run bringing the Giants within three after three quarters. The Jets responded with a drive of their own including several third down conversions but rookie Aaron Ross made the first of several big plays including a deep interception. The Giants drove 99 yards, which ended with a spectacular 53-yard touchdown catch and run by Plaxico Burress, who stiff-armed a Jets defender down the sideline. With the Jets driving for a score, Ross struck again, intercepting Pennington and returned it 43 yards to clinch the win. Brandon Jacobs notched his first ever 100-yard rushing performance, Manning managed 186 yards and 2 touchdowns despite a poor first half, [Osi Umenyiora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osi_Umenyiora "Osi Umenyiora") added a sack and [Sam Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Madison "Sam Madison") added his first interception of the season. The Giants had now won four straight regular season meetings against the Jets and improved to 3–2 on the season. ### Week 6: at Atlanta Falcons \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=17 "Edit section: Week 6: at Atlanta Falcons")\] The Giants cruised to their fourth straight win with an easy 31–10 victory over the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons") on _Monday Night Football_. After the Falcons moved the ball and scored three points on a 47-yard field goal by [Morten Andersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morten_Andersen "Morten Andersen"), the Giants took the lead on a five-yard [play-action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play_action "Play action") touchdown pass from [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") to [Amani Toomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amani_Toomer "Amani Toomer"). The Falcons responded as [Jerious Norwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerious_Norwood "Jerious Norwood") ran 67 yards untouched, putting the Falcons on top 10–7. New York responded with a quick six-play, 82-yard drive capped off by a 1-yard touchdown run by [Reuben Droughns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuben_Droughns "Reuben Droughns") for a 14–10. After the defense stopped Atlanta again, the Giants took command as Manning hit [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress") for his eighth and league-lead-tying touchdown from 42 yards out and a 21–10 lead. The Giants squandered several chances to add on more points as the team struggled moving at the end of the first half and Eli Manning threw a late interception. In the second half, the defense continued to dominate. [Fred Robbins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Robbins "Fred Robbins"), [Antonio Pierce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Pierce "Antonio Pierce") and [Justin Tuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Tuck "Justin Tuck") notched sacks for Big Blue and rookie [Aaron Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Ross "Aaron Ross") added his third interception in two weeks. The Giants added a [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes") field goal from 32 yards out for a 14-point lead, then capped off the win with a nine-yard touchdown run by [Derrick Ward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Ward "Derrick Ward"). On the night, the Giants rushed for 188 yards, Eli Manning passed for 303 yards along with a pair of touchdowns and interceptions and the defense shut down Atlanta following the slow start. Burress led the Giants with 97 receiving yards and Amani Toomer became the Giants all-time reception leader, catching 7 passes for 89 yards including his early touchdown. The Giants improved to 4–2 and took a four-game winning streak into the next week's game against the 49ers. * The Giants and Falcons series has now been won by the road team the last 12 meetings. * The Giants notched their 600th franchise win. * The 6.7 [Nielsen rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_ratings "Nielsen ratings") (8.48 million viewers) was the lowest in _Monday Night Football_ history, however it was the _highest_ rated cable program for the week. The decisive Game 4 of the [National League Championship Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_National_League_Championship_Series "2007 National League Championship Series") was played at the same time.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-variety-mnf-27) ### Week 7: vs. San Francisco 49ers \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=18 "Edit section: Week 7: vs. San Francisco 49ers")\] The Giants recorded their fifth straight victory with a convincing 33–15 win over the [San Francisco 49ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers") at Giants Stadium. Things started off well as the Giants drove right down the field on their opening possession. The balanced, well-executed seven-minute drive was capped off by a 4-yard touchdown pass from [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") to [Amani Toomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amani_Toomer "Amani Toomer"). The extra point was missed by [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes"). On their next possession, the Giants were driving for more, but a tipped ball resulted in an interception inside the red zone. The 49ers responded with a nice drive of their own, aided by a personal foul on linebacker [Antonio Pierce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Pierce "Antonio Pierce") and several third down conversions. San Francisco cashed in with a touchdown from [Trent Dilfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trent_Dilfer "Trent Dilfer") to [Arnaz Battle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnaz_Battle "Arnaz Battle"). Following a [Frank Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Gore "Frank Gore") fumble, the Giants took control. The running game, which accounted for 140 total yards helped the Giants move back in front. [Brandon Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jacobs "Brandon Jacobs") scored on a five-yard run for a 13–7 lead. After an interception by [Sam Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Madison "Sam Madison"), the Giants added a 30-yard field goal by Tynes. Tynes made it 19–7 at the half with another field goal, this time from 39 yards, inside the final minute. The Giants defense dominated in the second half, notching six sacks and four total turnovers. [Osi Umenyiora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osi_Umenyiora "Osi Umenyiora") put the game away with a sack, forced fumble, and 75-yard touchdown return up the field for a 26–7 lead. The Niners got two points back on a blocked punt out of the end zone but Antonio Pierce redeemed himself for two earlier personal fouls by intercepting Trent Dilfer and returning the ball inside the 10. After a flag on the 49ers, Manning threw his second touchdown, this time to [Jeremy Shockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Shockey "Jeremy Shockey") for a 33–9 lead. The 49ers scored late to provide the final points in the 33–15 win. On the day, Brandon Jacobs rushed for 107 yards, Manning completed 18 of 31 passes for nearly 150 yards with two touchdowns and an interception, and the defense notched six sacks: 2.5 for [Michael Strahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Strahan "Michael Strahan"), 1.5 for [Justin Tuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Tuck "Justin Tuck"), 1 for [Aaron Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Ross "Aaron Ross") and 1 for Umenyiora. Pierce and Madison provided the two Giants interceptions.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-28) For the fourth consecutive year under [Tom Coughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Coughlin "Tom Coughlin"), the Giants were 5–2 after seven games. ### Week 8: at Miami Dolphins (London) \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=19 "Edit section: Week 8: at Miami Dolphins (London)")\] The Giants got their sixth straight win with a rain-soaked 13–10 victory over the winless [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins") in the first International Series game, held at England's Wembley Stadium. Persistent rain throughout the day had soaked the field and hurt both teams on offense as the field was torn up for most of the afternoon, but the Giants survived to get to 6–2 on the season as they headed for their bye week. [![Image 11](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/47/Giants_jersey.jpg/330px-Giants_jersey.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Giants_jersey.jpg) A giant Giants jersey is unfurled on the field at Wembley Stadium After a missed Miami field goal on the opening drive of the game, the Giants traveled down the field, mixing up a combination of run and pass. [Brandon Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jacobs "Brandon Jacobs") had a big day, running in the rain for 131 yards on 23 carries. [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning"), who threw for only 59 yards in the game, missed a wide open [Amani Toomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amani_Toomer "Amani Toomer") in the end zone from inside the five, and the Giants had to settle for a 20-yard field goal from [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes"). The Giants extended their lead to 10 with a 14-play, 69-yard drive in the second quarter. Jacobs and [Reuben Droughns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuben_Droughns "Reuben Droughns") ran heavily on the drive and Eli Manning evaded the Dolphins defense, scrambling 10 yards for the game's first touchdown. After a [Cleo Lemon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleo_Lemon "Cleo Lemon") fumble, which was recovered by [Michael Strahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Strahan "Michael Strahan"), the Giants stretched the lead to 13 at the half with a 41-yard kick from Tynes. In the third quarter, after recovering a Manning fumble, the Dolphins drove the ball down inside the Giants 5. However, a Lemon muffed snap forced the Dolphins to kick a field goal. The Giants continued to run well with Jacobs, and had a chance to tack on 3 more points but Tynes missed badly on a 29-yard field goal. In the final two minutes, the Dolphins scored their first touchdown with [Ted Ginn Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Ginn_Jr. "Ted Ginn Jr.")'s first ever NFL touchdown reception. An attempted onside kick from [Jay Feely](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Feely "Jay Feely") skidded off the wet surface straight out of bounds, enabling the Giants to run out the clock for the win. For the day, Jacobs ran for his career-high 131 yards, and [Fred Robbins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Robbins "Fred Robbins") and [Kawika Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawika_Mitchell "Kawika Mitchell") recorded sacks. The Giants have won six in a row for the first time since 1994. Eli Manning scored the NFL's first regular season touchdown outside of North America. With their sixth-straight win, the Giants entered their bye week at 6–2.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-2007pfr-24) ### Week 10: vs. Dallas Cowboys \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=20 "Edit section: Week 10: vs. Dallas Cowboys")\] Coming off their bye week, the Giants went home, donned their alternate red uniforms, and played the [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys"). In the first quarter, New York trailed early as Cowboys quarterback [Tony Romo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Romo "Tony Romo") completed a 15-yard touchdown pass to tight end [Tony Curtis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Curtis_/(American_football/) "Tony Curtis (American football)"). The Giants responded as quarterback [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") completed an 8-yard touchdown pass to tight end [Jeremy Shockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Shockey "Jeremy Shockey"). In the second quarter, Dallas regained the lead as kicker [Nick Folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Folk "Nick Folk") made a 44-yard field goal. The Giants took the lead with running back [Reuben Droughns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuben_Droughns "Reuben Droughns") getting a 1-yard touchdown run. Afterwards, the Cowboys retook the lead with Romo completing a 20-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [Patrick Crayton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Crayton "Patrick Crayton"). Originally, the Giants were willing to be down by 3 at halftime. However, because a taunting penalty on Dallas linebacker [Kevin Burnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Burnett "Kevin Burnett") placed them near midfield, New York went for some points. The Giants tied the game with kicker [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes") making a 40-yard field goal. In the third quarter, Romo completed a 25-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [Terrell Owens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrell_Owens "Terrell Owens") and the Cowboys regained the lead. In the fourth quarter, the Giants made a 26-yard field goal from Tynes. Afterwards, Dallas' Romo and Owens hooked up with each other again on a 50-yard touchdown pass.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-29) With the loss, New York fell to 6–3, and were swept by the Cowboys for the first time since 2003. They have not worn their red uniforms since.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-2007pfr-24) During the season series against the Cowboys, the Giants pass defense allowed 8 passing touchdowns, despite only allowing 8 passing touchdowns from their previous opponents this year. ### Week 11: at Detroit Lions \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=21 "Edit section: Week 11: at Detroit Lions")\] The Giants flew to [Ford Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Field "Ford Field") for a Week 11 intraconference duel with the [Detroit Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Lions "Detroit Lions"). In the first quarter, New York took the early lead as kicker [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes") made a 28-yard field goal for the only score of the period. In the second quarter, the Giants increased their lead as quarterback [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") completed a 10-yard TD pass to running back [Brandon Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jacobs "Brandon Jacobs") for the only score of the period. In the third quarter, the Lions got on the board as kicker [Jason Hanson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Hanson "Jason Hanson") made a 42-yard field goal. New York would reply with Tynes kicking a 46-yard field goal. In the fourth quarter, the Giants improved their lead as Tynes made a 20-yard field goal. Detroit's quarterback [Jon Kitna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Kitna "Jon Kitna") completed a 35-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [Calvin Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Johnson "Calvin Johnson"). With the win, the Giants improved to 7–3.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-2007pfr-24) Linebacker [Mathias Kiwanuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathias_Kiwanuka "Mathias Kiwanuka") suffered a broken left fibula, ending his season. ### Week 12: vs. Minnesota Vikings \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=22 "Edit section: Week 12: vs. Minnesota Vikings")\] Coming off their road win over the Lions, the Giants went home for a Week 12 intraconference duel with the [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings "Minnesota Vikings"). In the first quarter, New York trailed early as Vikings quarterback [Tarvaris Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarvaris_Jackson "Tarvaris Jackson") completed a 60-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [Sidney Rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Rice "Sidney Rice"). The Giants responded with running back [Reuben Droughns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuben_Droughns "Reuben Droughns") getting a 1-yard touchdown run. Minnesota retook the lead with safety [Darren Sharper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darren_Sharper "Darren Sharper") returning an interception 20 yards for a touchdown. In the second quarter, Vikings' running back [Chester Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chester_Taylor "Chester Taylor") got an 8-yard touchdown run, along with kicker [Ryan Longwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Longwell "Ryan Longwell") making a 46-yard field goal. In the third quarter, Giants' kicker [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes") made a 48-yard field goal, and Minnesota's Longwell made a 26-yard field goal. In the fourth quarter, the Vikings' safety [Dwight Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Smith_/(American_football/) "Dwight Smith (American football)") returned an interception 93 yards for a touchdown, along with linebacker [Chad Greenway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad_Greenway "Chad Greenway") returning an interception 37 yards for a touchdown. New York's quarterback [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") completed a 6-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress") to complete the scoring. With the loss, the Giants fell to 7–4.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-2007pfr-24) Eli Manning was intercepted four times (with three of his interceptions being returned for touchdowns). He became the fourth quarterback in NFL history to have three interceptions get returned for touchdowns. His performance was all the more embarrassing as the Vikings had the league's worst pass defense in 2007 (albeit with the league's strongest run defense), and were playing in this game without starting corner [Antoine Winfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antoine_Winfield_Sr. "Antoine Winfield Sr."). ### Week 13: at Chicago Bears \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=23 "Edit section: Week 13: at Chicago Bears")\] Hoping to rebound after a loss to the Vikings, the Giants flew to [Soldier Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soldier_Field "Soldier Field") for a Week 13 intraconference duel with the defending NFC champion [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears"). In the first quarter, New York trailed early as Bears quarterback [Rex Grossman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Grossman "Rex Grossman") completed a 1-yard touchdown pass to tight end [Desmond Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desmond_Clark "Desmond Clark") for the only score of the period. In the second quarter, the Giants got on the board as running back [Derrick Ward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Ward "Derrick Ward") got a 2-yard touchdown run. Chicago responded with kicker [Robbie Gould](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Gould "Robbie Gould") getting a 35-yard and a 46-yard field goal. In the third quarter, the Bears increased their lead to 16–7 with Gould making a 41-yard field goal for the only score of the period. In the fourth quarter, New York scored touchdowns on their last two drives in the final 7 minutes; [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") completed a 6-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [Amani Toomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amani_Toomer "Amani Toomer") (initially ruled an incomplete pass that was challenged and overturned), then running back [Reuben Droughns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuben_Droughns "Reuben Droughns") got a 2-yard touchdown run. The Giants held on defensively and improved to 8–4 with the victory. Derrick Ward (24 carries for 154 yards and 1 touchdown) left the game in the fourth quarter with a fractured fibula, effectively ending his season. Excluding [Super Bowl XLII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII "Super Bowl XLII") two months later, [Michael Strahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Strahan "Michael Strahan") had his final career sack in the second quarter. ### Week 14: at Philadelphia Eagles \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=24 "Edit section: Week 14: at Philadelphia Eagles")\] Coming off their road win over the Bears, the Giants flew to [Lincoln Financial Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Financial_Field "Lincoln Financial Field") for a Week 14 NFC East rematch with the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles"). In the first quarter, New York trailed early as Eagles quarterback [Donovan McNabb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donovan_McNabb "Donovan McNabb") completed an 18-yard touchdown pass to running back [Brian Westbrook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Westbrook "Brian Westbrook") for the only score of the period. In the second quarter, the Giants started to draw close as kicker [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes") managed to get a 19-yard and a 23-yard field goal. In the third quarter, Philadelphia responded with kicker [David Akers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Akers "David Akers") getting a 29-yard field goal. Afterwards, New York took the lead with quarterback [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") completing a 20-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress"), along with Tynes kicking a 23-yard field goal. In the fourth quarter, the Eagles tried to come back as Akers nailed a 39-yard field goal. In the final seconds, Philadelphia had a chance to tie the game and force overtime. Fortunately for the Giants, Akers missed a 57-yard field goal off the right upright with 1 second left to preserve the victory and the season-sweep. With the win, the Giants improved to 9–4.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-2007pfr-24) This also marked the first time since their [Super Bowl XXXV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXV "Super Bowl XXXV") appearance of 2000 that New York had won 6-straight road games. As of 2025, this is the last time the Giants have swept the Eagles. ### Week 15: vs. Washington Redskins \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=25 "Edit section: Week 15: vs. Washington Redskins")\] Coming off their season-sweeping road win over the Eagles, the Giants went home for a Week 15 Sunday night NFC East rematch with the [Washington Redskins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Redskins "Washington Redskins"). In the first quarter, New York trailed early as Redskins kicker [Shaun Suisham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Suisham "Shaun Suisham") managed to get a 49-yard field goal for the only score of the period. In the second quarter, the Giants continued to trail as Suisham kicked a 31-yard field goal, along with running back [Ladell Betts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladell_Betts "Ladell Betts") getting a 14-yard touchdown run. New York would get on the board with kicker [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes") getting a 35-yard field goal. Washington would end the half with Suisham nailing a 28-yard field goal. In the third quarter, the Giants' deficit climbed as Redskins running back [Clinton Portis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_Portis "Clinton Portis") getting a 5-yard touchdown run (with a failed 2-point conversion). New York tried to make a comeback as quarterback [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") completed a 19-yard touchdown pass to tight end [Kevin Boss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Boss "Kevin Boss"). However, the wind and Washington's defense prevented any hopes. Eli Manning set a record of futility in the game with 35 incomplete passes, setting a record for most incomplete passes in an NFL game since the AFL–NFL merger. In fairness to Manning, his receivers also did not play well, dropping at least eight of his passes. Washington quarterback [Todd Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Collins_/(quarterback/) "Todd Collins (quarterback)"), making his first NFL start since 1997 in place of the injured [Jason Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Campbell "Jason Campbell"), didn't play much better, going 8–25, but got the win. With the loss, not only did the Giants fall to 9–5, but they also lost tight end [Jeremy Shockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Shockey "Jeremy Shockey") for the season in the third quarter with a broken left fibula. It would be his final appearance as a member of the Giants. Due to the Giants' increasing problems with Shockey's attitude and the emergence of [Kevin Boss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Boss "Kevin Boss") during the remainder of the season, he became expendable and was eventually traded to the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints"). ### Week 16: at Buffalo Bills \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=26 "Edit section: Week 16: at Buffalo Bills")\] The Giants took their 6–1 road record to Buffalo in search of clinching a playoff spot. They were able to rebound nicely from the week 15 home loss to Washington with a 38–21 win over the Bills. The Giants utilized their running game to wear down the Bills, as [Brandon Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jacobs "Brandon Jacobs") rushed for 143 yards and 2 touchdowns and rookie [Ahmad Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Bradshaw "Ahmad Bradshaw") rushed for 151 yards and a touchdown, including an 88-yard hustle that gave the Giants a 31–21 lead in the fourth quarter. Eli Manning had a rough day throwing the ball, as the harsh conditions forced him into completing just 7 of 16 passes and throwing for only 111 yards with two interceptions. [Kawika Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawika_Mitchell "Kawika Mitchell") and [Corey Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Webster "Corey Webster") also returned interceptions for touchdowns. The Giants rallied early from a 14–0, first-quarter deficit to win a game played through rain, wind, and snow. Early on, it appeared that the Bills would dominate the game, with [Trent Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trent_Edwards "Trent Edwards") finding [Michael Gaines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Gaines "Michael Gaines") for a three-yard touchdown to make it 7–0. After the Giants punted, Edwards hit [Lee Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Evans_/(American_football/) "Lee Evans (American football)") for a 4-yard touchdown to make it 14–0. As the weather changed from windy with no precipitation to windy and snowy, so did the Giants's fortunes. In the second quarter, [Brandon Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jacobs "Brandon Jacobs") ran for a six-yard touchdown, then on the next drive had his longest run of the season, a 43-yard touchdown run to tie the game at 14. A Lawrence Tynes field goal made it 17–14 at the half. In the third quarter, a [Marshawn Lynch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshawn_Lynch "Marshawn Lynch") touchdown run and a goal line stand by the Bills made the score 21–17 Bills heading into the final quarter. However, the Giants ran away with the contest in the fourth. With 14:05 to go in the 4th, Trent Edwards's pass was deflected and intercepted by linebacker (and future Bill) [Kawika Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawika_Mitchell "Kawika Mitchell"), who returned it 20 yards for a touchdown for the go-ahead score. With 6:27 to go, the Giants got the ball back on their own 12-yard line. During the second half, rookie 7th-round pick [Ahmad Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Bradshaw "Ahmad Bradshaw"), who seldom played outside of special teams before this game but who now had an opportunity due to [Derrick Ward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Ward "Derrick Ward")'s injury and [Reuben Droughns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuben_Droughns "Reuben Droughns")'s declining play, checked into the game. Bradshaw (who, unusual for a Giant, played with a single "y" on one side of his helmet instead of the standard "ny" in this game) received a handoff towards the left side of the line, cut towards the left sideline, received a key block from receiver [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress"), and sprinted down the sideline 88 yards for a touchdown to make it 31–21. Bradshaw's run is the third-longest in Giants history, with [Tiki Barber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiki_Barber "Tiki Barber")'s 95-yard touchdown against the Raiders on New Year's Eve 2005 being the longest. Just three plays later, Trent Edwards was intercepted by cornerback [Corey Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Webster "Corey Webster"), who returned Edwards's errant pass 34 yards for the game-clinching touchdown. While Eli Manning played poorly again, going 7–15 for just 111 yards with two interceptions and four fumbles (two lost), Trent Edwards also had a poor performance, going just 9-26 for 161 yards. Although he threw for 2 touchdowns, he also threw 3 interceptions (2 returned for touchdowns) and fumbled twice (though both were recovered by other Bills), and was just 3–19 after his first two drives. Ahmad Bradshaw ran for 151 yards on just 17 carries, while Brandon Jacobs ran for a career-high 143 yards on 25 carries with 2 touchdowns. Another important stat to note is that all 59 points in the game were scored going towards the east end zone. With the win, the Giants improved to 10–5 to clinch their third consecutive playoff berth. They also secured the 5th seed when the [Washington Redskins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Washington_Redskins_season "2007 Washington Redskins season") defeated the [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Minnesota_Vikings_season "2007 Minnesota Vikings season") later that night. [\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-30) ### Week 17: vs. New England Patriots \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_New_York_Giants_season&action=edit§ion=27 "Edit section: Week 17: vs. New England Patriots")\] This marked the first time since [Super Bowl I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_I "Super Bowl I") that an NFL game was simulcast by more than one television network. It was the first time an NFL game was carried on three national networks ([CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS"), [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC"), and [NFL Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Network "NFL Network")) with an additional 1.2 million viewers seeing the game on local stations in New York and Massachusetts. The game was originally scheduled to be broadcast on NFL Network only, but [Roger Goodell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Goodell "Roger Goodell") allowed CBS and NBC to broadcast with NFL Network it due to the Patriots being 15–0 and needing just one more win to become the first team to go 16–0 in the regular season. There was disagreement surrounding head coach [Tom Coughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Coughlin "Tom Coughlin")'s decision to play all his starters. Some of them played injured, notably [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress") who had an ankle injury and missed most of practice during the end of the season and the Giants postseason run. A Giants win would have no effect in the playoffs the following Sunday, as the Giants had earned the #5 seed as a wildcard and Dallas had won the division with the best record in the NFC. By playing his starters, he risked losing additional players on an already banged up roster playing against a heavily favored Patriots team, which was playing for the history books to go undefeated in the regular season. Still, the Giants were the final team to have a chance to end the Patriots' shot at a perfect season, and a victory would be an impressive display for pride and momentum. The Patriots set numerous offensive records while becoming the first ever 16–0 team in the regular season in a raucous and hostile [Giants Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants_Stadium "Giants Stadium"). [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady") set a single season record for touchdown passes, [Randy Moss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Moss "Randy Moss") set a record for touchdown receptions, and the Patriots as a whole set a record for most points scored. Despite losing 38–35, the Giants played well and impressed critics in the defeat. [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") played well, completing 22 of 32 passes for 251 yards while throwing 4 touchdowns and 1 interception, the lone interception of the game. The Giants led 28–16 in the third quarter, the Patriots' largest deficit this season. Also, Brandon Jacobs reached 1,000 yards rushing after gaining 67 yards on the ground on 15 carries. With the loss, the Giants ended the regular season at 10–6, with a road playoff game set on January 6 against the [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers "Tampa Bay Buccaneers"). The game became in retrospect a preview of [Super Bowl XLII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII "Super Bowl XLII"). In the end, 15.7 million viewers watched the game on CBS, 13.2 million on NBC, 4.5 million on the NFL Network, and 1.2 million on New York, Boston and [Manchester, New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester,_New_Hampshire "Manchester, New Hampshire") television stations.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#cite_note-32) The
