**Super Bowl XLII** was an [American football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") game between the [National Football Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_Conference "National Football Conference") (NFC) champion [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season "2007 New York Giants season") and the [American Football Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Football_Conference "American Football Conference") (AFC) champion [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_England_Patriots_season "2007 New England Patriots season") to decide the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) champion for the [2007 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_NFL_season "2007 NFL season"). The game was played on February 3, 2008, at the [University of Phoenix Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Farm_Stadium "State Farm Stadium") in [Glendale, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glendale,_Arizona "Glendale, Arizona").[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-10) This Super Bowl was a rematch of the [final game of the regular season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_England_Patriots%E2%80%93New_York_Giants_game "2007 New England Patriots–New York Giants game"), in which the Patriots won, 38–35. The Giants defeated the heavily favored Patriots by a score of 17–14, widely considered one of the biggest [upsets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upset_/(sport/) "Upset (sport)") in the history of professional North American sports.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-13) Giants quarterback [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning"), who completed 19 of 34 passes for 255 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, was named [Super Bowl MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_MVP "Super Bowl MVP"). The Patriots entered the game as 12-point favorites after becoming the first team to complete a [perfect regular season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfect_season "Perfect season") since the [1972 Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Miami_Dolphins_season "1972 Miami Dolphins season"), and the only one since the league expanded to a 16-game regular season schedule in 1978. The Giants, who finished the regular season with a 10–6 record, were seeking to become the first NFC [wild card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_card_/(sports/) "Wild card (sports)") team to win a [Super Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl "Super Bowl"), and were also looking for their seventh championship and first since they won [Super Bowl XXV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXV "Super Bowl XXV") seventeen years earlier. The game was tight throughout, with both teams' defense dominating the competition until near the end of the game. The fourth quarter saw a Super Bowl-record three lead changes. After [David Tyree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Tyree "David Tyree")'s 3-yard touchdown reception at the beginning of the quarter, Patriots wide receiver [Randy Moss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Moss "Randy Moss") made a 6-yard touchdown reception, making the score 14-10 with 2:42 left in the game. The Giants started their subsequent drive on their own 17-yard line with 2:39 left.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-14)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-15) On the drive's most memorable play, Tyree made the "[Helmet Catch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmet_Catch "Helmet Catch")" on 3rd down, a leaping one-handed catch pinning the football with his right hand to the crown of his helmet for a 32-yard first down conversion.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-16)[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-17) After a second first-down conversion by [Steve Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Smith_/(wide_receiver,_born_1985/) "Steve Smith (wide receiver, born 1985)") on 3rd and 11, wide receiver [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress") scored the game-winning touchdown on a 13-yard reception. The Patriots then proceeded to [turnover on downs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turnover_on_downs "Turnover on downs") on their final drive as the Giants ran out the clock. The game became one of the lowest scoring Super Bowls since [Super Bowl IX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_IX "Super Bowl IX") 31 years earlier; it would be followed by [Super Bowl LIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIII "Super Bowl LIII") in 2019, a game that also involved the Patriots. This game was also the first, and as of the [2024 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NFL_season "2024 NFL season"), only, Super Bowl with three fourth-quarter lead changes. Super Bowl XLII is often considered the greatest Super Bowl of all time in retrospect by several media outlets.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-18)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-19)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-20)[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-21)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-22) The Giants' victory is remembered as one of the greatest "[Cinderella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underdog "Underdog")" stories in professional sports history,[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-23)[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-24)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-25) and their game-winning drive is regarded as one of the greatest of all time.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-26) Several outlets and sports publishers have also considered the game to be a moment that defined [sports in the 2000s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000s_in_sports "2000s in sports").[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-27)[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-28)[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-29)[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-30)[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-31)[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-32) Super Bowl XLII was ranked fifth on the NFL's 100 Greatest Games list, the highest ranked Super Bowl game,[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-33) while Tyree's catch was ranked third on the NFL's 100 Greatest Plays.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-34) The game's broadcast on [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_on_Fox "NFL on Fox") broke the then-record for the most watched Super Bowl in history with an average of 97.5 million viewers in the United States.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-viewers-8) The Giants and Patriots would once again meet in [Super Bowl XLVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLVI "Super Bowl XLVI") four years later, where the Giants would win again 21–17. ### Host selection process \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Super_Bowl_XLII&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: Host selection process")\] As always, the league considered several potential host cities before choosing the [Phoenix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix,_Arizona "Phoenix, Arizona") area. In this case, the process drew special interest because the league considered holding Super Bowl XLII in New York City or Washington, D.C. as a symbol of the recovery from the [September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks "September 11 attacks").[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-35) New York City's bid did not go far. Aside from the obvious climatic concerns, it was also difficult to find a suitable stadium. Proposed renovations to the 1970s-vintage [Giants Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants_Stadium "Giants Stadium") were still being disputed amongst the various parties. Giants Stadium also lacked a roof, as did both of New York City's baseball stadiums, and the NFL had never played an outdoor Super Bowl in a cold weather climate. The city of New York and the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets") failed to secure a deal to build a new [West Side Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Side_Stadium "West Side Stadium") (which, according to the initial plans, would have been built with a roof).[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-36) During the years since the Super Bowl XLII bid fell through, Giants Stadium has been demolished. Its replacement, [MetLife Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MetLife_Stadium "MetLife Stadium"), was awarded [Super Bowl XLVIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLVIII "Super Bowl XLVIII"). Washington, D.C.'s bid proved to be more viable as the D.C. area had a relatively new (albeit roofless) stadium in [FedExField](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FedExField "FedExField"). DC's winter weather, although still potentially problematic, is milder than New York's climate. In the end, the process boiled down to three finalists: Washington, D.C., Phoenix and Tampa. NFL owners finally chose [University of Phoenix Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Phoenix_Stadium "University of Phoenix Stadium") in [Glendale, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glendale,_Arizona "Glendale, Arizona") as the site for Super Bowl XLII during their October 30, 2003, meeting in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago").[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-37) In subsequent years, [Raymond James Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_James_Stadium "Raymond James Stadium") in Tampa was chosen as the site for [Super Bowl XLIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLIII "Super Bowl XLIII") and the proposed (but never built) [West Side Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Side_Stadium "West Side Stadium") was briefly designated as the venue for [Super Bowl XLIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLIV "Super Bowl XLIV"). However, this game was later moved to [Sun Life Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Life_Stadium "Sun Life Stadium") in [Miami Gardens, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Gardens,_Florida "Miami Gardens, Florida"), when it became clear that the new stadium in New York City would not be built in time for the February 2010 game. [![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/University_of_Phoenix_Stadium_no_field.jpg/250px-University_of_Phoenix_Stadium_no_field.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:University_of_Phoenix_Stadium_no_field.jpg) [University of Phoenix Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Phoenix_Stadium "University of Phoenix Stadium") The [kickoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kickoff_/(American_football/) "Kickoff (American football)") for the game took place at 4:32 p.m. [MST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_Time_Zone "Mountain Time Zone") (23:32 [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time "Coordinated Universal Time")). This was the first [Super Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl "Super Bowl") played on a retractable natural-grass field surface; the University of Phoenix Stadium's removable surface is unique among American sports venues.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-38) Super Bowl XLII was also the second Super Bowl played in a [retractable-roof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retractable_roof "Retractable roof") stadium (the first was played at [Reliant Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reliant_Stadium "Reliant Stadium") in Houston for [Super Bowl XXXVIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXVIII "Super Bowl XXXVIII")). During the regular season, the home team decides 90 minutes before kickoff whether the roof will be open or closed, and an open roof must remain open unless weather conditions get worse. However, as a neutral site, the NFL controls the option to open or close without any restrictions. The first time this was employed was in [Super Bowl XXXVIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXVIII "Super Bowl XXXVIII") at [Reliant Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reliant_Stadium "Reliant Stadium"); the roof was open for pregame and halftime shows and closed during the game.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-39) Because there was rain in the forecast for Super Bowl XLII, the roof was closed for the entire day's activities. During a February 6, 2007, ceremony with Arizona Governor [Janet Napolitano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Napolitano "Janet Napolitano"), the [NFL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") and the Arizona Super Bowl Host Committee unveiled the slogan "Who Wants It More?" along with its mascot "Spike the Super Ball" (an [anthropomorphized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropomorphism "Anthropomorphism") football with sunglasses and sneakers) and a large "Super Bowl XLII Countdown Clock" at [Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Sky_Harbor_International_Airport "Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport").[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-sloganUnveiled-40) The Super Bowl XLII logo was also unveiled. It features the shape of the state of [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona "Arizona") in red and two horizontal white stripes in the middle to represent the vertical lines on University of Phoenix Stadium. The turquoise Roman numerals represent the Native American culture of Arizona. The red star represents the AFC and the blue star represents the NFC.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-sloganUnveiled-40) This was also the last Super Bowl with the league's previous logo painted at midfield; the following season, the league redesigned its primary logo.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-41) [![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/2012_Packers_vs_Giants_-_Eli_Manning_3.jpg/250px-2012_Packers_vs_Giants_-_Eli_Manning_3.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2012_Packers_vs_Giants_-_Eli_Manning_3.jpg) QB [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") was named Super Bowl MVP The Giants began the season with low expectations after star running back [Tiki Barber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiki_Barber "Tiki Barber") retired. The Giants had lost in the NFC Wild Card round in each of the previous two seasons and had not won a playoff game in seven years. Quarterback [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning"), the younger brother of [Super Bowl XLI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLI "Super Bowl XLI") [MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_MVP "Super Bowl MVP") quarterback [Peyton Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peyton_Manning "Peyton Manning"), had struggled to find consistency. In his three seasons as a starter, he had completed less than 54% of his passes with a career passer rating of 73.4. While generally regarded as a solid quarterback, Manning had been unable to achieve the same level of success as fellow 2004 draftees [Philip Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Rivers "Philip Rivers") (for whom he was traded) and [Ben Roethlisberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Roethlisberger "Ben Roethlisberger"), the latter of whom had already won a Super Bowl ([Super Bowl XL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XL "Super Bowl XL")). By the 2007 season, many sports writers were starting to question if Eli would ever live up to the expectations that accompanied being selected with the first overall pick in a draft.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-news-42) The criticism of Manning intensified as the Giants lost the first two games of the regular season. The Giants recovered, though, notching six consecutive wins and finishing the year with a 10–6 record. The Giants were able to secure a wild card bid in the playoffs, despite the loss of running back [Derrick Ward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Ward "Derrick Ward"), defensive end [Mathias Kiwanuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathias_Kiwanuka "Mathias Kiwanuka"), and four-time Pro Bowl tight end [Jeremy Shockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Shockey "Jeremy Shockey") to injury. In the final game of the regular season, the Giants played at home against the undefeated New England Patriots. Although the Giants had already earned a playoff spot and had nothing to gain by winning the game, Giants head coach Tom Coughlin decided to play his starters throughout the game. The Giants, clearly playing to win against the league's best team, narrowly lost 38–35. But the effort seemed to rejuvenate the Giants and prepare them for a difficult playoff run. Manning led his team to three road playoff wins against the [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers_season "2007 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season"), [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2007 Dallas Cowboys season") and [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season "2007 Green Bay Packers season") respectively, without throwing a single interception. The Giants' three playoff wins gave them an NFL record 10 consecutive wins on the road. They finished the season with a franchise-low 77 penalties, after setting a franchise record two years before with 146. Manning finished the 2007 season with 3,336 yards, 23 touchdowns, and 20 interceptions.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-43) His primary target, [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress"), caught 70 passes for 1,050 yards and 12 touchdowns. [Amani Toomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amani_Toomer "Amani Toomer"), the Giants all-time leading receiver and one of only two players remaining from their last Super Bowl appearance in [Super Bowl XXXV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXV "Super Bowl XXXV"), was also a reliable target with 59 receptions for 760 yards, while Shockey contributed 57 receptions for 619 yards and 3 touchdowns before suffering a season-ending injury in week 15. The Giants' ground game was led by running back [Brandon Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jacobs "Brandon Jacobs"), who at 6 ft 4 in (193 cm) and 264 pounds (120 kg), was one of the largest starting halfbacks in the NFL. He finished the season with 1,009 yards and an average of five yards per carry, while also catching 23 passes despite starting only nine games. Running back [Reuben Droughns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuben_Droughns "Reuben Droughns") rushed for 276 yards and team-leading 6 touchdowns, while also catching 7 passes for 49 yards and returning 21 kickoffs for 437 yards. Rookie running back [Ahmad Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Bradshaw "Ahmad Bradshaw") added 38 kickoff returns for 921 yards, while also rushing for 190. The Giants had a defensive line that was led by defensive ends [Osi Umenyiora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osi_Umenyiora "Osi Umenyiora") (the lone [Pro Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl "Pro Bowl") representative on the team, the fewest a Super Bowl team has ever had), [Michael Strahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Strahan "Michael Strahan"), and [Justin Tuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Tuck "Justin Tuck"). Umenyiora led the defense with 13 sacks and five forced fumbles. Strahan, another veteran from the [Giants' last Super Bowl appearance in 2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_New_York_Giants_season "2000 New York Giants season"), had nine sacks, giving him a career total of 141.5 and breaking the franchise record held by [Lawrence Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Taylor "Lawrence Taylor"). Tuck recorded ten sacks and 48 solo tackles. In the secondary, cornerback [Sam Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Madison "Sam Madison") and safety [Gibril Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibril_Wilson "Gibril Wilson") led the team with four interceptions each. Cornerback [R. W. McQuarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R._W._McQuarters "R. W. McQuarters") had no interceptions during the season, but played effectively in the playoffs, with interceptions in each of the Giants first three postseason games. Punter [Jeff Feagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Feagles "Jeff Feagles") played in his first Super Bowl after 20 years in the NFL. This was also the last game for Giants athletic trainer [John Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Johnson_/(trainer/) "John Johnson (trainer)") who had been with the team for 60 years. The Giants became only the fourth team to win the Super Bowl without playing a single home game in the preceding playoffs. They joined the [1966 Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_Green_Bay_Packers_season "1966 Green Bay Packers season") (who won [Super Bowl I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_I "Super Bowl I") against the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_Kansas_City_Chiefs_season "1966 Kansas City Chiefs season")), the [1969 Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_Kansas_City_Chiefs_season "1969 Kansas City Chiefs season") (who won [Super Bowl IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_IV "Super Bowl IV") against the [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_Minnesota_Vikings_season "1969 Minnesota Vikings season")) and the [2005 Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Pittsburgh_Steelers_season "2005 Pittsburgh Steelers season") (who won [Super Bowl XL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XL "Super Bowl XL") against the [Seattle Seahawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Seattle_Seahawks_season "2005 Seattle Seahawks season")) in accomplishing this feat. However, the Packers had to win two games (including the Super Bowl), the Chiefs three, and the Steelers and the Giants four, in order to accomplish this. Since then, two other teams also won three road playoff games to reach the Super Bowl: the [2010 Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Green_Bay_Packers_season "2010 Green Bay Packers season"), who won [Super Bowl XLV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLV "Super Bowl XLV") over the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Pittsburgh_Steelers_season "2010 Pittsburgh Steelers season"), and the [2020 Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers_season "2020 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season"), winners of [Super Bowl LV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LV "Super Bowl LV") (played in their home stadium with limited attendance because of [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19")) over the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Kansas_City_Chiefs_season "2020 Kansas City Chiefs season"). The Giants were the only NFC team to make multiple Super Bowl appearances in the 2000s decade, at the ends of the 2000 and 2007 seasons. Starting with the [Rams' appearance in 2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXVI "Super Bowl XXXVI"), ten different NFC teams represented the conference from 2001 to 2010: [St. Louis Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_St._Louis_Rams_season "2001 St. Louis Rams season"), [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers_season "2002 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season"), [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Carolina_Panthers_season "2003 Carolina Panthers season"), [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Philadelphia_Eagles_season "2004 Philadelphia Eagles season"), [Seattle Seahawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Seattle_Seahawks_season "2005 Seattle Seahawks season"), [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Chicago_Bears_season "2006 Chicago Bears season"), [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season "2007 New York Giants season"), [Arizona Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Arizona_Cardinals_season "2008 Arizona Cardinals season"), [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_New_Orleans_Saints_season "2009 New Orleans Saints season"), and [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Green_Bay_Packers_season "2010 Green Bay Packers season"). #### New England Patriots \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Super_Bowl_XLII&action=edit§ion=6 "Edit section: New England Patriots")\] [![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/TomBrady.jpg/250px-TomBrady.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TomBrady.jpg) QB [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady") threw a then NFL record 50 touchdowns during the regular season When the Patriots arrived at Super Bowl XLII, they were already billed as the greatest team in NFL history. In fact, the Patriots were the #1 team for every week of 2007, starting with the preseason all the way to the Super Bowl. The Patriots were not only competing for a fourth Super Bowl title since the 2001 season; they were aiming to become the first team in NFL history to achieve a 19–0 record. Their perfect 16–0 record in the regular season was the first since the league moved to a 16-game regular season in [1978](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_NFL_season "1978 NFL season"). It was also only the fourth undefeated and untied regular season in NFL history. New England set NFL records with 589 points scored (an average of 36.8 points per game) (since broken by the [2013 Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Denver_Broncos_season "2013 Denver Broncos season")), 75 total touchdowns, and a net differential of +315 points (they gave up 274 points, fourth best in the league). Some experts have suggested that the Patriots' 16–0 record is the culmination of a larger trend towards better records for top NFL teams since the [league realignment in 2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_NFL_season#Expansion_and_realignment "2002 NFL season").[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-44) [![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Randy-Moss_8-28-09_Patriots-vs-Redskins.jpg/250px-Randy-Moss_8-28-09_Patriots-vs-Redskins.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Randy-Moss_8-28-09_Patriots-vs-Redskins.jpg) WR [Randy Moss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Moss "Randy Moss") caught a league-record 23 touchdowns in 2007–08 The team was led by then eighth-year quarterback [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady") who proceeded to have the best season of his entire career and won his first [NFL MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "NFL Most Valuable Player Award") and [NFL Offensive MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Offensive_Player_of_the_Year_Award "NFL Offensive Player of the Year Award") awards, throwing for a then-career-high 4,806 yards and a then NFL record 50 touchdowns (22 more than his previous best season; since broken by Peyton Manning in [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Denver_Broncos_season "2013 Denver Broncos season")), and just eight interceptions. His passer rating of 117.2 was the second-highest season rating in NFL history. One often-cited reason for Brady's improved numbers was the acquisition of receivers [Randy Moss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Moss "Randy Moss") and [Wes Welker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Welker "Wes Welker").[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-msn-45) The Patriots acquired Moss, a nine-year veteran, from the [Oakland Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Raiders "Oakland Raiders") for a fourth-round pick in the [2007 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_NFL_draft "2007 NFL draft") after Moss had, statistically, the worst year of his career (with 42 receptions for 553 yards and three touchdowns). With the Patriots, though, Moss caught 98 receptions for 1,493 yards and an NFL record 23 touchdowns, and was selected a first-team All Pro. The Patriots also gave the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins") second- and seventh-round picks for Welker. Welker tied for the league lead with 112 receptions for 1,175 yards and 8 touchdowns, while also returning 25 punts for 249 yards and 7 kickoffs for 176, earning himself second-team All Pro selection. Welker and Moss both earned votes for [Offensive Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League_Offensive_Player_of_the_Year_Award "National Football League Offensive Player of the Year Award"). Other major contributors to the Patriots' passing game included [Donté Stallworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dont%C3%A9_Stallworth "Donté Stallworth"), who added 697 yards and three touchdowns, and tight end [Benjamin Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Watson "Benjamin Watson"), whose 36 receptions totaled 389 yards and six touchdowns. Running back [Laurence Maroney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Maroney "Laurence Maroney") was the Patriots' top rusher with 835 yards and six touchdowns, while [Sammy Morris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sammy_Morris "Sammy Morris") added 385 yards and three touchdowns (Morris ended up on injured reserve midway through the season, and thus could not play in the Super Bowl). Longtime Patriot [Kevin Faulk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Faulk "Kevin Faulk") had 265 yards and was also a reliable receiver out of the backfield, catching 47 passes for 383 yards and a touchdown. The Patriots' offensive line featured three players selected to the Pro Bowl, guard [Logan Mankins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan_Mankins "Logan Mankins"), tackle [Matt Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Light "Matt Light"), and center [Dan Koppen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Koppen "Dan Koppen"). The Patriots' defensive line was led by nose tackle [Vince Wilfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Wilfork "Vince Wilfork"), who was selected to his first [Pro Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl "Pro Bowl"); he was also fined four times during the season for unnecessary roughness.[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-wilforkfines-46) The Patriots had a set of veteran linebackers who had a combined 16 Pro Bowl selections. Outside linebacker [Mike Vrabel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Vrabel "Mike Vrabel") had, statistically, the best season of his career. He led the team in sacks with a career-high 12.5, while also forcing five fumbles and earning his first Pro Bowl selection. [Adalius Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adalius_Thomas "Adalius Thomas"), an off-season signing from the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens"), recorded six sacks. [Junior Seau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_Seau "Junior Seau"), who had been selected to the Pro Bowl 12 times during his career but had never won a Super Bowl, returned for his 18th season and got 74 tackles with 3.5 sacks. [Tedy Bruschi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tedy_Bruschi "Tedy Bruschi") recorded 92 tackles and two sacks. The Patriots' secondary featured another player selected to the Pro Bowl, cornerback [Asante Samuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Samuel "Asante Samuel"), who led the team with six interceptions. Defensive back [Ellis Hobbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellis_Hobbs "Ellis Hobbs") returned 35 kickoffs for 911 yards and a touchdown, ranking him 7th in the NFL with a 26.0 yards per return average. The Giants became the first NFC team (third overall) to advance to the Super Bowl by winning three playoff games on the road. After beating the fourth-seeded [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers_season "2007 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season") 24–14, the Giants upset the top-seeded [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2007 Dallas Cowboys season") 21–17, when R. W. McQuarters intercepted a pass from Cowboys quarterback [Tony Romo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Romo "Tony Romo") in the end zone as time expired. The Giants advanced to the Super Bowl with a 23–20 overtime win over the second-seeded [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season "2007 Green Bay Packers season") in the [NFC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_NFL_playoffs#NFC:_New_York_Giants_23,_Green_Bay_Packers_20_\(OT\) "2007–08 NFL playoffs"), which was the third coldest game in NFL history (−1 °F at kickoff, −24 °F wind chill) with an interception by [Corey Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Webster "Corey Webster") that set up [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes")'s game-winning 47-yard field goal. The field goal was the longest by a visiting kicker in [Lambeau Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambeau_Field "Lambeau Field") postseason history. This turned out to be the final game [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") played for the Packers. Meanwhile, the Patriots continued to set NFL records on their road to the Super Bowl. First, Brady set the NFL record for completion percentage in a single game (92.9%) with 26 of 28 completions for 268 yards and three touchdowns in their 31–20 win over the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Jacksonville_Jaguars_season "2007 Jacksonville Jaguars season") in the divisional round, while safety [Rodney Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_Harrison "Rodney Harrison") tied an NFL record by recording an interception in his fourth consecutive postseason game. One week later, the Patriots defeated the [San Diego Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_San_Diego_Chargers_season "2007 San Diego Chargers season") 21–12 in the [AFC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_New_England_Patriots_21,_San_Diego_Chargers_12 "2007–08 NFL playoffs"). Although Brady threw three interceptions in the game, the Patriots defense forced two turnovers and limited the Chargers to four field goals, while Maroney rushed for 122 yards and a touchdown for the second game in a row. This was the sixth meeting between teams from [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") and [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") for a [major professional sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_professional_sports_leagues_in_the_United_States_and_Canada "Major professional sports leagues in the United States and Canada") championship. This previously occurred in two [Stanley Cup Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Cup_Finals "Stanley Cup Finals") ([1929](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1929_Stanley_Cup_Finals "1929 Stanley Cup Finals"), [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Stanley_Cup_Finals "1972 Stanley Cup Finals")) and three [World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Series "World Series") ([1912](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1912_World_Series "1912 World Series"), [1916](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1916_World_Series "1916 World Series"), [1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_World_Series "1986 World Series")).[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-47) The Patriots were heavily favored to win the game and become the first NFL team to go through a 16-game regular season and postseason undefeated. Had the Patriots won, they would also have joined the [1972 Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Miami_Dolphins_season "1972 Miami Dolphins season") as the only teams ever to win the NFL league championship with an undefeated and untied record. However, others predicted that the Giants could accomplish a win. The Giants' record of 10 consecutive road wins included five teams favored to beat them. The Giants achieved playoff victories against the [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2007 Dallas Cowboys season") (who had defeated the Giants twice in the regular season) and the [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers "2007 Green Bay Packers") (who had beaten the Giants in week 2).[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-SI-48) The Patriots and Giants had played against each other in the last week of the regular season. Technically, the game had little significance, since both teams had already clinched their respective spots in the playoffs. But due to the Patriots' quest for an undefeated season, this game was one of the most heavily watched games in league history. [NFL Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Network "NFL Network") was originally scheduled to air the game as part of their _[Saturday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thursday_Night_Football "Thursday Night Football")_ coverage, with [WCVB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WCVB-TV "WCVB-TV") and [WWOR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWOR-TV "WWOR-TV") carrying the game locally in Boston and New York. Shortly before the game was scheduled to air, [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_on_CBS "NFL on CBS") and [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC_Sunday_Night_Football "NBC Sunday Night Football") bought broadcast rights to the game and NFL Network's broadcast was carried by both networks, marking the first time in NFL history that an NFL game was carried on three broadcast networks at the same time. The game was also the first NFL game to be simulcast on a national level since [Super Bowl I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_I "Super Bowl I"). As they were favored to do, the Patriots won the game to finish the regular season undefeated. Still, the game was close and competitive, with both teams playing their starters for all 60 minutes. The Patriots won, 38–35, by overcoming a 12-point deficit in the third quarter, the largest deficit the Patriots had faced all season. "There is nothing but positives", Giants head coach [Tom Coughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Coughlin "Tom Coughlin") said after the game. "I told the players in playing this game everything would be positives, there would be no negatives and that is how I feel. I don't know any better way to be prepared for the playoffs than to go against a team that was 15–0."[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-nfl-49) This would be the third time in the Giants' four Super Bowl appearances in which the team played its eventual AFC opponent during that year's regular season. Both of the prior occasions saw the Giants beat those opponents in the Super Bowl (defeating the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Denver_Broncos_season "1986 Denver Broncos season") in [Super Bowl XXI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXI "Super Bowl XXI") and the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_Buffalo_Bills_season "1990 Buffalo Bills season") in [Super Bowl XXV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXV "Super Bowl XXV")). For the third consecutive year, the arrival dates for the teams were staggered, with the Patriots arriving on Sunday, January 27 (corresponding to the traditional day that teams arrive for the game with the two-week break) and the Giants waiting to arrive until Monday, January 28. A report filed by [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN")'s [Rachel Nichols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Nichols_/(journalist/) "Rachel Nichols (journalist)") suggested that the Giants stayed to practice more of their game plan in their home facility before arriving at the Super Bowl. By electing to stay back at home the Giants chose to follow a tactic that the previous two Super Bowl champions, the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Indianapolis_Colts_season "2006 Indianapolis Colts season") (before [Super Bowl XLI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLI "Super Bowl XLI")) and the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Pittsburgh_Steelers_season "2005 Pittsburgh Steelers season") (before [Super Bowl XL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XL "Super Bowl XL")), had employed. The Patriots practiced at [Sun Devil Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Devil_Stadium "Sun Devil Stadium") on the campus of [Arizona State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_State_University "Arizona State University"), while the Giants practiced at the [Arizona Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Cardinals "Arizona Cardinals")' practice facility, both of which are located in [Tempe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempe,_Arizona "Tempe, Arizona"). As the [designated home team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl#Home_team_designation "Super Bowl") in the annual rotation between AFC and NFC teams, the Patriots elected to wear their home navy uniforms with silver pants, while the Giants wore their road white uniforms with grey pants. [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_on_Fox "NFL on Fox") broadcast Super Bowl XLII as part of an annual cycle between the three main broadcast television partners of the NFL. [Joe Buck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Buck "Joe Buck") and [Troy Aikman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troy_Aikman "Troy Aikman") called the game, while [Pam Oliver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pam_Oliver "Pam Oliver") and [Chris Myers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Myers "Chris Myers") were the sideline reporters.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-fox-pr-7) Fox aired nine hours of pre-game programming, which began with a special episode of _[Fox News Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_News_Sunday "Fox News Sunday")_, as well as a two-hour special (_Fox Super Sunday_) hosted by [Fox News Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_News_Channel "Fox News Channel") anchor [Shepard Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shepard_Smith "Shepard Smith"), which previewed the [Super Tuesday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Tuesday "Super Tuesday") [primaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_primary "United States presidential primary") for the [2008 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election "2008 United States presidential election").[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-50) The _[Fox NFL Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_NFL_Sunday "Fox NFL Sunday")_ panel hosted the main pre-game show, led by [Curt Menefee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curt_Menefee "Curt Menefee"), joined by [Terry Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Bradshaw "Terry Bradshaw"), [Howie Long](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howie_Long "Howie Long"), and [Jimmy Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Johnson_/(American_football_coach/) "Jimmy Johnson (American football coach)"). [Jillian Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jillian_Barberie "Jillian Barberie") served as Weather and entertainment reporter, [Frank Caliendo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Caliendo "Frank Caliendo") appeared in various comedic skits (including one where he portrayed [John Madden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Madden "John Madden") and correctly predicted that the Giants would win) and _[American Idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Idol "American Idol")_ host [Ryan Seacrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Seacrest "Ryan Seacrest") provided coverage of celebrity arrivals to the game site. A Spanish language broadcast was aired on the second audio program with John Laguna as play-by-play announcer and Pepe Mantilla as color analyst.[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-51) The telecast was the most watched Super Bowl in history with an average of 97.5 million viewers in the United States. These numbers were later surpassed by several subsequent games, including 2015's [Super Bowl XLIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLIX "Super Bowl XLIX") (which was also hosted by Glendale), which now holds the record with an average of 114 million viewers.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-52) The Super Bowl XLII broadcast achieved the highest [Nielsen ratings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_ratings "Nielsen ratings") (43.3) for the game since [Super Bowl XXXIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXIV "Super Bowl XXXIV"). At the time, it was also the second [most watched TV program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_watched_television_broadcasts "List of most watched television broadcasts") of all time in the United States.[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-53) Fox took in at least $250 million in revenue from [commercial time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_ads "Super Bowl ads") sold for the game.[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-54) One of 63 thirty-second spots among thirty-seven different advertisers cost an estimated $2.7 million (excluding production costs),[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-ad-9) up from $2.6 million in 2007. However, advertisers are usually offered discounted rates below the official one.[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-55) As Super Bowl XLII fell only two days before Super Tuesday, critics and politicians foresaw the possibility that presidential candidates could attempt to buy time during the Super Bowl. However, Fox stated that it would not accept such ads, citing both [equal time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equal_time "Equal time") regulations (the [FCC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Communications_Commission "Federal Communications Commission") has additionally ruled that, despite requirements for all broadcasters to provide "reasonable" access to commercial inventory for candidates before an election or primary, candidates cannot reasonably expect to receive ad time during high-profile programs of this nature), and the fact that all of the spots had already been sold out by January 2008.[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-56) However, the campaign of Democratic candidate [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") did purchase local ad time in some markets.[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-57) The rock band [Eels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eels_/(band/) "Eels (band)") announced an intent to broadcast a one-second spot during the game (consisting solely of lead singer [Mark Oliver Everett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Oliver_Everett "Mark Oliver Everett") saying the letter "U") to promote its compilation album "[Useless Trinkets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Useless_Trinkets:_B-Sides,_Soundtracks,_Rarities_and_Unreleased_1996%E2%80%932006 "Useless Trinkets: B-Sides, Soundtracks, Rarities and Unreleased 1996–2006")", but later announced that it had backtracked after having learned it could only purchase commercial time in 30-second blocks (and a proposal to recruit 29 other advertisers to air their own one-second ads alongside them could be harmful to viewers with [photosensitive epilepsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosensitive_epilepsy "Photosensitive epilepsy")).[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-58) Outside North America, Super Bowl XLII was distributed by the NFL and NFL International. Overall, the game was available to an estimated potential audience of one billion viewers within 223 countries and territories.[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-59) However, viewing figures outside North America rose only marginally on previous years with an estimated 10 million people tuning in from outside the United States, Canada and Mexico for an overall global audience in the region of 114 million.[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-223_countries-60) [Dick Stockton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Stockton "Dick Stockton") and [Sterling Sharpe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sterling_Sharpe "Sterling Sharpe") were the announcers for the International broadcast.[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-61) The [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") acquired the rights in the United Kingdom. After the game, New York City erupted in celebration, with the sounds of cheers and honking horns echoing through city streets. Crowds of elated New Yorkers, surprised by their team's unexpected victory, packed Second Avenue in [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), stalling traffic around the borough.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-76) [Times Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Square "Times Square") was swarmed with celebrating Giants fans well past midnight; similar celebrations arose throughout [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"), [Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens "Queens"), [The Bronx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bronx "The Bronx"), [Staten Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island "Staten Island"), [Long Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island "Long Island"), [Westchester County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westchester_County,_New_York "Westchester County, New York"), [Fairfield County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairfield_County,_Connecticut "Fairfield County, Connecticut"), and [North Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Jersey "North Jersey"), where the Giants play their home games.[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-Celebrations-77) New York Mayor [Michael Bloomberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bloomberg "Michael Bloomberg"), witnessing the first New York sports team championship victory as mayor, praised the hometown team's upset victory, saying; "New York has come back many times in the past, and Big Blue proved tonight that you should never, ever, count us out." Many New Yorkers polled the Giants' win to be among the most satisfying championship victories in New York sports history.[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-78) There were also a series of firsts with the championship, not just for the Giants, but also for the city of New York and the [New York metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_metropolitan_area "New York metropolitan area"). Those firsts were: * Giants: * Super Bowl championship since [Super Bowl XXV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXV "Super Bowl XXV") in 1991. * City of New York: * Super Bowl championship since the Giants won Super Bowl XXV in 1991. * Major professional sports championship since: * The [Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Yankees "New York Yankees") won the [2000 World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_World_Series "2000 World Series"). * This was also the first championship for a team other than the Yankees since the [Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Rangers "New York Rangers") won the [1994 Stanley Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Stanley_Cup_Finals "1994 Stanley Cup Finals"). * New York Metropolitan area: * Super Bowl championship since the Giants win in 1991. regular season meeting, the teams scored a mere 10 points by the end of the third quarter, with the Patriots leading 7–3. The Patriots' record-setting offense gave up five sacks and one lost fumble, while the Giants' offense managed only five first downs in the second and third quarters. Yet in the fourth quarter, [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") threw two touchdown passes, including the winning drive that culminated with a 13-yard touchdown pass to [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress") with 35 seconds remaining. The Giants won the coin toss and started the game with the longest drive in Super Bowl history,[\[83\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-83) a 16-play, 63-yard march that consumed 9 minutes, 59 seconds, breaking their own record of 9 minutes, 29 seconds set in [Super Bowl XXV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXV "Super Bowl XXV"), and featured four third-down conversions, the most ever on a Super Bowl opening drive. But the Patriots halted the drive at their own 14-yard line, forcing the Giants to settle for a 32-yard field goal from kicker [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes") that gave the Giants a 3–0 lead. The Patriots responded with their own scoring drive, as running back [Laurence Maroney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Maroney "Laurence Maroney") returned the kickoff 43 yards to his own 44-yard line, after which he rushed twice for 14 yards. Quarterback [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady") then completed three passes for 23 yards, but after two incomplete passes, the Patriots were faced with 3rd-and-10 on the New York 17-yard line. However, on that play, Giants linebacker [Antonio Pierce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Pierce "Antonio Pierce") committed pass interference by striking the helmet of tight end [Benjamin Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Watson "Benjamin Watson") in the end zone, setting up 1st-and-goal for the Patriots at the 1-yard line. Two plays later, on the first play of the second quarter, Maroney scored on a 1-yard touchdown run, giving the Patriots their first lead of the game, 7–3. The two teams each only had one drive in the entire opening quarter, a Super Bowl record. It was the first Super Bowl since [Super Bowl XXXIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXIII "Super Bowl XXXIII") in which both teams scored on their initial possession of the game. On the Giants' first drive of the second quarter, on 3rd-and-7, wide receiver [Amani Toomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amani_Toomer "Amani Toomer") caught a deep pass from quarterback [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") along the left sideline while dragging his feet in bounds for a 38-yard gain, moving the ball to the Patriots' 19-yard line. But three plays later, Manning threw a pass that bounced out of the arms of wide receiver [Steve Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Smith_/(wide_receiver,_born_1985/) "Steve Smith (wide receiver, born 1985)") and into the hands of cornerback [Ellis Hobbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellis_Hobbs "Ellis Hobbs") for an interception. The Patriots' ensuing drive resulted in a three-and-out as on 3rd-and-1 safety [James Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Butler_/(American_football/) "James Butler (American football)") and defensive end [Michael Strahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Strahan "Michael Strahan") (who was playing in his final game) tackled Maroney for a 2-yard loss and the Patriots were forced to punt. Then on the Giants' next drive, running back [Ahmad Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Bradshaw "Ahmad Bradshaw") fumbled a hand-off from Manning and linebacker [Pierre Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Woods "Pierre Woods") appeared to recover the ball at the Giants' 30-yard line. But after the officials picked through the pile, it was determined that Bradshaw had made the recovery. The Giants maintained possession and still had to punt. The Patriots' next drive ended with back-to-back 7-yard sacks, the first by linebacker [Kawika Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawika_Mitchell "Kawika Mitchell"), and the second by defensive end [Justin Tuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Tuck "Justin Tuck"). On the Giants' next drive, they moved the ball to the Patriots' 25-yard line, but linebacker [Adalius Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adalius_Thomas "Adalius Thomas") sacked Manning and forced a fumble. Smith recovered the ball, but Bradshaw was flagged for illegally batting the ball forward before the recovery. The penalty pushed the Giants out of field goal range, and following an incompletion, they were forced to punt again. After the punt, two 18-yard receptions by wide receivers [Randy Moss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Moss "Randy Moss") and [Donté Stallworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dont%C3%A9_Stallworth "Donté Stallworth") moved the ball to the Giants' 44-yard line. But with 22 seconds left before halftime, Tuck strip-sacked Brady and defensive end [Osi Umenyiora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osi_Umenyiora "Osi Umenyiora") recovered the ball. The game then went to halftime with the Patriots leading 7–3. On the first drive of the second half, the Patriots had a 4th-and-2 and chose to punt. However, after the kick, Patriots head coach [Bill Belichick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Belichick "Bill Belichick") challenged that the Giants' defense had 12 players on the field and replay confirmed that was the case as Giants linebacker [Chase Blackburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chase_Blackburn "Chase Blackburn") was unable to get to the sidelines as the ball was being snapped. Therefore, referee [Mike Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Carey_/(American_football/) "Mike Carey (American football)") reversed the play, and the Giants were penalized for having too many players on the field, giving the Patriots a new set of downs. The Patriots then drove to the Giants' 25-yard line, but Strahan sacked Brady for a 6-yard loss on third down (which was Strahan's final career sack), bringing up 4th-and-13 on the Giants' 31-yard line. Belichick decided against a 49-yard field goal attempt by kicker [Stephen Gostkowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Gostkowski "Stephen Gostkowski") (near Gostkowski's season long of 50 yards) and tried to pick up a first down instead. Brady's pass to wide receiver [Jabar Gaffney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jabar_Gaffney "Jabar Gaffney") was incomplete as it went out of the back of the end zone and the Giants took over on downs. After the teams traded punts going into the fourth quarter, Manning completed a 45-yard pass to tight end [Kevin Boss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Boss "Kevin Boss"). Following three runs by Bradshaw for 13 yards and a 17-yard reception by Smith on third down, Manning finished the 6-play, 80-yard drive with a 5-yard touchdown pass to usually unheralded wide receiver [David Tyree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Tyree "David Tyree"), giving the Giants a 10–7 lead with 11:05 left in the game. After the teams exchanged punts again, the Patriots got the ball at their own 20-yard line with 7:54 remaining. Brady then completed a 5-yard pass to wide receiver [Wes Welker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Welker "Wes Welker") and a 10-yard pass to Moss, followed by a 9-yard run by Maroney to give the Patriots a first down at their own 44-yard line. Brady followed with a 13-yard pass to Welker, a 4-yard completion to running back [Kevin Faulk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Faulk "Kevin Faulk"), and then a 10-yard pass to Welker for a first down at the Giants' 29-yard line. After that, Brady found Moss for an 11-yard completion and Faulk for a 12-yard completion and New England now had 1st-and-goal from the Giants' 6-yard line. Following two incomplete passes, cornerback [Corey Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Webster "Corey Webster") slipped while backing into coverage, leaving Moss wide open in the end zone where Brady found him for a 6-yard touchdown to give the Patriots a 14–10 lead with 2:42 left in the game.[\[84\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-84) On the ensuing kickoff, safety [Raymond Ventrone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Ventrone "Raymond Ventrone") leveled wide receiver [Domenik Hixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domenik_Hixon "Domenik Hixon") after a 14-yard return, giving the Giants the ball on their own 17-yard line with 2:39 left and all three timeouts remaining. Following two receptions by Toomer for 20 yards, running back [Brandon Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jacobs "Brandon Jacobs") kept the drive alive with a crucial 2-yard run off guard on 4th-and-1. Manning picked up 5 yards with a scramble on the next play. Then on 2nd-and-5, Manning’s pass was high and behind Tyree, but fell harmlessly out of bounds as Patriots cornerback [Asante Samuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asante_Samuel "Asante Samuel") could not corral the pass for the potential game-ending interception. Play-by-play announcer [Joe Buck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Buck "Joe Buck") was quick to note Manning’s visible frustration at the apparent miscommunication with Tyree on the play, which stopped the clock with 1:15 remaining. On the next play, 3rd-and-5 from the Giants' 44-yard line, Manning found himself in trouble as the Patriots' pass rush got to him quickly after the snap. He eluded Adalius Thomas, who missed Manning despite having the clearest shot at him, and then broke free from the grasp of defensive ends [Jarvis Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jarvis_Green "Jarvis Green") and [Richard Seymour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Seymour "Richard Seymour"), both of whom had the quarterback by the jersey but failed to hold him in the grasp. In what is considered to be among the greatest Super Bowl plays of all time, Manning then re-oriented himself and launched the ball deep down the middle of the field, where both Tyree and Patriots safety and multiple-time Pro Bowler [Rodney Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_Harrison "Rodney Harrison") were in position to make a play on the ball. Tyree outjumped Harrison to secure the ball, and maintained possession by [pinning the ball against his helmet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmet_Catch "Helmet Catch") as he fell to the ground, clearly maintaining control for a gain of 32 yards and keeping the drive alive. Three plays later, on 3rd-and-11, Manning found a wide-open Smith for a 12-yard gain to the Patriots' 13-yard line, and Smith stepped out of bounds to stop the clock. On the next play, Hobbs was beaten badly to the outside by the 6'6" wide receiver [Plaxico Burress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaxico_Burress "Plaxico Burress") on a "slant-and-go" route, allowing Manning more than enough room to find his big-bodied target for the touchdown. The score capped a 12-play, 83-yard drive to give the Giants a 17–14 lead and prompted a roar from the fans in Glendale, then a mere 35 seconds from potentially witnessing the first 19–0 perfect season.[\[85\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-85) The Patriots attempted one last desperate drive to either tie or win the game from their own 26-yard line with 29 seconds remaining and all three of their timeouts, but the Giants' defense did not allow a single yard. Following an errant pass attempt by Brady, defensive tackle [Jay Alford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Alford "Jay Alford") sacked Brady for a 10-yard loss. The following play, a deep pass to Moss, was knocked away by cornerback [Corey Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Webster "Corey Webster"), and Brady's 4th-and-20 Hail Mary pass in Moss' direction was batted down by safety [Gibril Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibril_Wilson "Gibril Wilson"), sealing the upset victory for the Giants. After the incompletion, it appeared that the officials would run out the clock, as it briefly read zero, before one second was re-added.[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-86) Coaches, players, reporters, and fans crowded the field as if the game had ended. Belichick hugged Giants head coach [Tom Coughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Coughlin "Tom Coughlin") at midfield, then left for the locker room. This early departure was later criticized by some sportswriters, but other reporters defended Belichick by noting that he did not snub Coughlin (which would have been surprising anyway because the two coaches were friends from their days working together for [Bill Parcells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Parcells "Bill Parcells") in the 1980s) and that the outcome of the game had been decided.[\[87\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-87)[\[88\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-88) The delay lasted 2 minutes and 27 seconds before For other American football terms, see [Glossary of American football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_American_football "Glossary of American football"). | 17 | 14 | | ### Statistical overview \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Super_Bowl_XLII&action=edit§ion=29 "Edit section: Statistical overview")\] Manning completed 19 of his 34 passes for 255 yards, including a mark of 9-of-14 for 152 yards and two touchdowns in the fourth quarter, with one interception, to be named the game's [Most Valuable Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_MVP "Super Bowl MVP").[\[90\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-90) Manning also became the first quarterback to throw two go-ahead touchdowns in the fourth quarter of a Super Bowl. Toomer was the Giants' leading receiver, with 6 catches for 84 yards, and Bradshaw and Jacobs rushed for 45 and 42 yards, respectively. Burress had only 2 receptions for 27 yards, but one of those was the game-winning touchdown with 35 seconds left. The Patriots' offense recorded 274 total yards to the Giants' 338. While he never scored, Welker tied a Super Bowl record with 11 receptions for 109 yards. Moss had five catches for 62 yards and a touchdown, and Maroney rushed for 36 yards and a touchdown. Brady completed 29 of his 48 passes for 266 yards and a touchdown. Brady's 29 completions gave him a career total of 100 in his four Super Bowls, surpassing the previous record for Super Bowl completions that was held by Joe Montana at 83. Justin Tuck and Adalius Thomas were the top defensive performers for the Giants and Patriots, respectively, as each recorded five solo tackles, two sacks, and one forced fumble. One key fact of the game was the number of possessions that reached the red-zone: the Giants made it four times and their defense limited the Patriots to two. The Patriots had six consecutive possessions that came short of reaching the Giants' 20-yard line. The game was the first Super Bowl in which neither team rushed for as many as 100 yards, with the Patriots held to 45.[\[91\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-pfr_sb_XLII-91) The Giants became the first team to win a Super Bowl in 3 different decades (1986, 1990, 2007). The Giants set an NFL record with 11 consecutive road wins in a single season. The Giants' matchup in [Week 8 vs. the Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_York_Giants_season#Week_8:_at_Miami_Dolphins_\(London\) "2007 New York Giants season") in London was an official Giants road game because it was originally scheduled to be played at [Dolphin Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_Rock_Stadium "Hard Rock Stadium"). The Giants were also officially classified as the "road" team for Super Bowl XLII based on the annual Super Bowl rotation where the NFC champions serve as the away team in even-numbered years, and as such, this was the Giants first championship game won on the road.[\[92\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-92) Also note that the Week 5 game vs. the New York Jets was considered a "home" game for the Giants. Patriots receiver [Wes Welker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Welker "Wes Welker") tied the record for most catches in a Super Bowl, with 11. Welker was the fourth player to record 11 receptions in a Super Bowl, following [Dan Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Ross_/(American_football/) "Dan Ross (American football)") of the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bengals "Cincinnati Bengals") in [Super Bowl XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XVI "Super Bowl XVI"), [Jerry Rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Rice "Jerry Rice") of the [San Francisco 49ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers") in [Super Bowl XXIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXIII "Super Bowl XXIII"), and [Deion Branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deion_Branch "Deion Branch") of the Patriots in [Super Bowl XXXIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXIX "Super Bowl XXXIX"). [Demaryius Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demaryius_Thomas "Demaryius Thomas") in [Super Bowl XLVIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLVIII "Super Bowl XLVIII") would set a new record for catches. With his fourth quarter touchdown pass to Moss, Brady became just the fourth quarterback with a touchdown pass in four different Super Bowls, joining [Roger Staubach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Staubach "Roger Staubach"), [Joe Montana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Montana "Joe Montana") and [Terry Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Bradshaw "Terry Bradshaw"). He also became the sixth quarterback to start at least four Super Bowls, joining Montana, Bradshaw, Staubach, [Jim Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Kelly "Jim Kelly") and [John Elway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Elway "John Elway"). The Giants opening drive consumed 9 minutes and 59 seconds, making it the longest drive in Super Bowl history.[\[93\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-93) The drive was 27 seconds longer than the previous record, which the Giants had set in winning [Super Bowl XXV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXV "Super Bowl XXV") against the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bills "Buffalo Bills"). Due to the length of the Giants' opening drive (which itself contained a record 4 third-down conversions), the first quarter featured only two possessions, a record for an opening quarter.[\[94\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-94) The three lead changes in the fourth quarter were also a Super Bowl record.[\[95\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-95) Although not a record, the 17 points scored by the Giants was the fewest points for a Super Bowl victor since [Super Bowl IX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_IX "Super Bowl IX").[\[96\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII#cite_note-96) This was the seventh consecutive Super Bowl where one team made the first score and the opponent made the second; that is a record.
