420km 261miles ![Image 8](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ab/Green_pog.svg/20px-Green_pog.svg.png) Packers ![Image 9](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Blue_pog.svg/20px-Blue_pog.svg.png) Giants The **Giants–Packers rivalry** is a [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) [rivalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League_rivalries "National Football League rivalries") between the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants") and the [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers").[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-4) The two teams have played since 1970 in the [National Football Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_Conference "National Football Conference"), and they play each other in the regular season either every three years and once every six seasons at each team's home stadium or depending on its NFC division placement, and in the postseason.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-operations.nfl.com_creating_schedule-5)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-:0-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-:1-7)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-:2-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-:3-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-auto-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-13) Notable games and moments ------------------------- The [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") and [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants") have played 64 games including 26 games that have been decided by 8 points or less:[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-14) Below are eight notable games from the rivalry. * In the [1938 NFL Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1938_NFL_Championship_Game "1938 NFL Championship Game"), the Giants and Packers met in their first playoff game. It was a battle between an 8–3 Packers team and an 8–2–1 Giants team. The Giants took an early 9–0 lead, but the Packers got a pair of touchdowns in the second quarter to make it 16–14 at the half. The Giants played well on defense in the second half, holding the Packers to 3 points. They won their third championship in their history, 23–17, and their first playoff game against Green Bay.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-15) * In the [1944 NFL Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1944_NFL_Championship_Game "1944 NFL Championship Game"), the Giants and Packers met in their third playoff game. It was a battle between two teams that got 8 wins in the regular season, with the Giants being 8–1–1 and the Packers being 8–2. The Packers scored two touchdowns in the second quarter and never looked back. They held a shutout through 3 quarters, and won the game 14–7. The Packers overall playoff record against the Giants is now 2–1.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-16) * In the [1962 NFL Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_NFL_Championship_Game "1962 NFL Championship Game"), the Giants and Packers played their last playoff game until 2007. The Packers were 13–1 while the Giants were 12–2. The Giants didn't score until the third quarter, but still were within 6 heading into the final quarter. However, the Packers got a game-sealing field goal in the 4th quarter to secure a 16–7 win. The Packers improved to 4–1 against the Giants in the playoffs.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-17) * In [1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_NFL_season "1971 NFL season"), the Giants and Packers met for the first time in the 1970s. The Packers got a 100 yard field goal return in the first quarter to take a 7–0 lead. The Giants then went on a 28–0 run, that included two [Fran Tarkenton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran_Tarkenton "Fran Tarkenton") touchdown passes, a defensive touchdown, and a special teams touchdown. The Packers got a touchdown at the end of the half to make it 28–14. It was a blowout heading into the fourth quarter as the Giants led 42–24. The Packers got a couple touchdowns and a safety to make it 42–40, but came up just short in the highest scoring game of the rivalry. For the Giants, Fran Tarkenton threw for 4 touchdown passes and had a 120.2 rating.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-18) * In the [2007 NFC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_NFC_Championship_Game "2007 NFC Championship Game"), The Packers and Giants met in their first playoff battle since 1962. The game was -1°F at kickoff, one of the coldest in NFL playoff history.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-19) The Packers were favored to win as they finished 13–3 to the Giants 10–6. Two [Lawrence Tynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Tynes "Lawrence Tynes")' field goals gave the Giants a 6–0 lead with 11:41 in the 2nd quarter. The Packers got a quick response with a [Donald Driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Driver "Donald Driver") 90 yard touchdown catch and led 10–6 at halftime. The teams got off to hot offensive starts to the second half, as the Giants won the 3rd Quarter with 14 points to the Packers’ 7, now ahead 20-17. [Brandon Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jacobs "Brandon Jacobs"), [Donald Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Lee_/(American_football/) "Donald Lee (American football)") and [Ahmad Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Bradshaw "Ahmad Bradshaw") were the players who scored touchdowns in the 3rd quarter. With 11:46 left in the 4th quarter, the Packers tied the game on a [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") 37 yard field goal. The game remained tied at 20 for the rest of regulation, so it went into overtime. The Packers won the toss, but [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") threw an interception to [Corey Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Webster "Corey Webster"), who got 9 yards on the return into Packers territory. This was Brett Favre's last pass as a Packer. Even though the Giants went three and out, they were in field goal range. Lawrence Tynes, who missed two field goals earlier, was the man who got the 47 yard field goal to win the game. This NFC Championship game sent the Giants to the Super Bowl where they pulled off a huge upset and beat the 16–0 [Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_New_England_Patriots "2007 New England Patriots") by the score of 17–14.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-20) * In [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NFL_season "2011 NFL season"), the Packers and Giants battled it out in December as they played in an important regular season game. The Giants were 6–5 heading into the game, while the Packers were still undefeated at 11–0. [Eli Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") and [Aaron Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers "Aaron Rodgers") both threw a touchdown pass in the first quarter, as the Giants led 10–7 at the end of this quarter. On the first play of the second quarter, [Clay Matthews III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay_Matthews_III "Clay Matthews III") returned an interception 38 yards for a touchdown. The Packers and Giants then traded touchdowns at the end of the half to make it 21–17 Green Bay. In the third quarter, [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings") and [Hakeem Nicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hakeem_Nicks "Hakeem Nicks") caught touchdowns to make it 28–24 at the end of the quarter. In the fourth quarter, the Giants trailed 35–27 inside the two minute warning, but Eli Manning led a drive that was capped off by a Hakeem Nicks touchdown catch. The Giants got the two point conversion to tie the game at 35 with 58 seconds left. However, on the final drive of the game, Aaron Rodgers completed a 24 yard pass to [Jermichael Finley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jermichael_Finley "Jermichael Finley") and a 27 yard pass to [Jordy Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordy_Nelson "Jordy Nelson") to get Green Bay well into field goal range. Mason Crosby finished it off with a game winning field goal with no time left to win it 38–35 for Green Bay.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-21) * In the [2011 NFC Divisional round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011-12_NFL_playoffs "2011-12 NFL playoffs"), the Giants looked for revenge from their Week 13 loss to Green Bay. The Giants were heavy underdogs, finishing the regular season at just 9–7 to the Packers’ 15–1. The game was a fast start for the Giants, as after the teams traded field goals Eli Manning found Hakeem Nicks for a 66 yard touchdown to give the Giants a 10–3 lead at the end of the first quarter. [John Kuhn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kuhn "John Kuhn") then caught an 8 yard touchdown early in the second quarter to tie the game at 10. It was 13–10 Giants with one play left in the first half. Eli Manning completed a 37 yard [Hail Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hail_Mary_pass "Hail Mary pass") touchdown pass to Hakeem Nicks to give the Giants a 20–10 lead just before the half. The Packers fell behind 30–13 but did get a touchdown from Aaron Rodgers to Donald Driver with 4:46 left in the fourth quarter. However, the hope for Green Bay was short lived, as the Giants only took 2 minutes and 10 seconds to make it a three score game. The game ended with the Giants winning 37–20, as they moved on to the NFC Championship Game. The Giants eventually won [Super Bowl XLVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLVI "Super Bowl XLVI") against the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_New_England_Patriots "2011 New England Patriots") 21–17.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-22) [![Image 10: Packers and Giants players lining up on the field near the end zone](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Giants_vs_Packers_Jan_8_2017.jpg/250px-Giants_vs_Packers_Jan_8_2017.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Giants_vs_Packers_Jan_8_2017.jpg) The Packers offense lining up against the Giants defense during their Wild Card playoff game. * In the [2016 Wild Card round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016-17_NFL_playoffs "2016-17 NFL playoffs"), the Packers and Giants played their most recent playoff game. The Packers finished 2016 with a 10–6 record while the Giants finished the season at 11–5. However the game was on the Packers’ home turf as they won their division, while the Giants finished behind the [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2016 Dallas Cowboys season") in their division. It was a slow start for Green Bay as they fell behind 6–0. The Packers got their first points with 2:20 left in the second quarter, as Aaron Rodgers completed a 5 yard touchdown pass to [Davante Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davante_Adams "Davante Adams"). This started giving Green Bay offensive momentum. Similarly to the 2011 Divisional round between these teams, there was one play left in the first half, and it was a Hail Mary. Aaron Rodgers, who completed two Hail Maries in 2015, completed another one from 42 yards away to [Randall Cobb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randall_Cobb_/(American_football/) "Randall Cobb (American football)") to give Green Bay a 14–6 lead before halftime. The Packers offense continued their dominance, scoring 24 points in the second half. The Giants defense, which was the second best in points allowed, never gave up 30 points in the regular season, but allowed 38 in this game. Aaron Rodgers finished with 362 yards and 4 touchdowns in the win. The Packers went on to beat the Cowboys 34–31 in the Divisional Round, before losing to the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Atlanta_Falcons "2016 Atlanta Falcons") 44–21 in the NFC Championship Game.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-23) * In the Packers' first international game in franchise history,[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry#cite_note-24) the 3-1 Giants faced the Packers, also 3-1, as 8 point underdogs. The Packers expectedly started strong by claiming a 0-10 lead with a Mason Crosby 46 yard field goal and an Aaron Rodgers 4 yard touchdown throw to [Allen Lazard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Lazard "Allen Lazard"). The Giants answered with a [Graham Gano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Gano "Graham Gano") 48 yard field goal to close the first quarter, resulting in a 3-10 score. The Packers would immediately respond on their subsequent drive with a Rodgers 2 yard touchdown to [Marcedes Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcedes_Lewis "Marcedes Lewis"), increasing the Packers' lead to 3-14.This would be the last touchdown the Packers would score in the contest. Giants quarterback [Daniel Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Jones_/(American_football/) "Daniel Jones (American football)") then lead an 86 yard drive culminating in a 2 yard rushing touchdown by [Daniel Bellinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bellinger "Daniel Bellinger"). With 1:15 left in the half, Rodgers would lead the Packers to a 48 yard field goal to close the half at 10-20. The Giants started the second half by scoring a 37 yard field goal, making the score 13-20. More importantly, their defense shut out the Packers for the rest of the game, while the Giants offense slowly chipped away at their deficit. After forcing a punt, the Giants then conducted a long 92 yard drive ending with a [Gary Brightwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Brightwell "Gary Brightwell") 2 yard touchdown. New York then forced a three and out and had a 60 yard drive ending with a [Saquon Barkley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saquon_Barkley "Saquon Barkley") rushing touchdown. Green Bay, finding themselves behind for the first time in the contest, attempted to lead a game-tying touchdown drive down 27-20 with 6:08 left in the fourth quarter. Rodgers lead Green Bay to the Giants' six yard line, but New York's defense forced an incompletion on 4th and 2 with 1:02 left in the contest. The Giants would then intentionally allow a [safety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_/(gridiron_football_score/) "Safety (gridiron football score)") to run out the clock, giving Rodgers the ball back with 0:11 left in the game. However, on his [Hail Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hail_Mary_pass "Hail Mary pass") attempt, Rodgers was sacked by [Oshane Ximines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oshane_Ximines "Oshane Ximines"), and New York completed their upset over Green Bay with a final score of 27–22. Packers on offense at home to the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") in week 11 The **2007 Green Bay Packers season** was the franchise's 89th overall and 87th season in the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). The Packers finished the regular season with a 13–3 record and clinched their first winning season, playoff appearance and division title since [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Green_Bay_Packers_season "2004 Green Bay Packers season"). They received for the first time since [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Green_Bay_Packers_season "1997 Green Bay Packers season") a [bye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bye_/(sports/) "Bye (sports)") for the first round of the [playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_playoffs,_2007%E2%80%9308 "NFL playoffs, 2007–08"), and won their divisional round playoff game to advance to the franchise's first [NFC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_Championship_Game "NFC Championship Game") in 10 years. The Packers ultimately lost the NFC Championship game to the eventual [Super Bowl champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLII "Super Bowl XLII") [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants"). It was the first time the Packers had lost a home NFC Championship game, and only their third home playoff loss ever. This was the last season for quarterback [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") as a Green Bay Packer, as he initially retired following the season but came out of retirement and was subsequently traded to the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_New_York_Jets_season "2008 New York Jets season") during the offseason. This season also marked the 50th anniversary of the opening of the Packers' home stadium of [Lambeau Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambeau_Field "Lambeau Field"). The Packers' tenure at Lambeau, now at 64 seasons, is the longest in NFL history at a single stadium, breaking the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears")' previous record of 50 seasons at [Wrigley Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrigley_Field "Wrigley Field") (1921–1970). On February 2, 2007, [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") announced that he would return for the 2007 season. "I am so excited about coming back," the 37-year-old quarterback said on the website of _[The Sun Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sun_Herald "The Sun Herald")_ in [Biloxi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biloxi "Biloxi"), [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi "Mississippi"). He also commented, "We have a good nucleus of young players. We were 8–8 last year, and that's encouraging."[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-returnNFL.com-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-returnPackers.com-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-returnSunHerald-3) Ted Thompson, Green Bay's general manager, confirmed the news, saying, "The Packers are excited by his decision and look forward to a successful 2007 campaign."[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-tedthompson-4) This would be, however, Brett Favre's last season with the Packers, after 16 years on the team. The [2007 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_NFL_draft "2007 NFL draft") occurred on April 28–29. The Packers picked 16th overall, selecting [defensive tackle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defensive_tackle "Defensive tackle") [Justin Harrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Harrell "Justin Harrell") in the first round.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-draftorder-5)

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=11 "Edit section: Regular season results")\] ### Week 1: vs. Philadelphia Eagles \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=12 "Edit section: Week 1: vs. Philadelphia Eagles")\] The Packers began their season at home against the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles"). In the first quarter, Green Bay's [Jarrett Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jarrett_Bush "Jarrett Bush") recovered the Eagles' [Greg Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Lewis_/(wide_receiver/) "Greg Lewis (wide receiver)")'s muffed punt in the end zone for a touchdown. The contest was tied in the closing minutes but the Eagles again muffed a punt return, setting up a 42-yard kick from Packers rookie kicker [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby"). This was the only game the Packers did not score an offensive touchdown. Crosby was named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-SpecialTeamsPlayeroftheWeek-13) Crosby is the only player in league history to boot a 50-plus-yard field goal and game winning field goal in the final minute in his first NFL game.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-Onlykicker-14) ### Week 2: at New York Giants \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=13 "Edit section: Week 2: at New York Giants")\] [![Image 14](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/GBNYShotgun.jpg/250px-GBNYShotgun.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GBNYShotgun.jpg) The Packers in the [shotgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shotgun_formation "Shotgun formation") Playing a close game until the fourth quarter, the Packers took a commanding lead late in the game (racking up 21 points in the final fifteen minutes) and winning the game 35–13. Early in the 4th quarter, Favre capped off a drive with a pass to the outside of the endzone to Donald Lee, and then followed it up with a 10-yard pass to Donald Driver by the goalpost for a score after the Giants fumbled the ensuing kickoff deep in their own territory. In the victory, Brett Favre threw for 286 yards and 3 touchdowns and gave him his 149th career win as a starter, the most by any [quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") in NFL history, surpassing [John Elway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Elway "John Elway"). Favre was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week for games played September 16–17.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-PlayeroftheWeek-15) Mike McCarthy was voted the Motorola NFL Coach of the Week.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-CoachoftheWeek-16) ### Week 3: vs. San Diego Chargers \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=14 "Edit section: Week 3: vs. San Diego Chargers")\] Quarterback Brett Favre threw three touchdown passes against the [Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Chargers "San Diego Chargers") in the victory, bringing his career total to 420 and tying [Dan Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino")'s career touchdown record. With just over two minutes remaining in the game and San Diego leading 21–17, Favre found wide receiver [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings") for a 57-yard catch and run across the middle of the field for the go-ahead score. On the Chargers ensuing drive, linebacker Nick Barnett intercepted a [Philip Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Rivers "Philip Rivers") pass and returned it to the San Diego 1-yard line setting up the Packers final score and a 10-point lead. Barnett was voted the GMC Defensive Player of the Week for games played on September 23 – 24.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-DefensivePlayeroftheWeek-17) This win made the Packers the only team to have missed the playoffs the previous season to return to open 3–0 against teams that made the playoffs the year before.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-first3and0-18) ### Week 4: at Minnesota Vikings \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=15 "Edit section: Week 4: at Minnesota Vikings")\] [![Image 15](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/09.30.07_favre_421TD.JPG/250px-09.30.07_favre_421TD.JPG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:09.30.07_favre_421TD.JPG) [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") broke [Dan Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino")'s TD pass record during Week 4 at the HHH Metrodome Coming off their home win over the Chargers, the Packers flew to the [Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubert_H._Humphrey_Metrodome "Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome") for an NFC North division game against [Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings "Minnesota Vikings"). In the first quarter, QB [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") threw a 16-yard TD pass to WR [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings") surpassing [Dan Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino") as the league's all-time leader in touchdown passes. He also became the league leader in pass attempts (8,393 at game's end).[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-PassAttemptLeader-19) Favre was named the NFC Offensive Player of the Week for the second time this season, having thrown for 344 yards and two touchdowns.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-PlayerOfTheWeek2-20) With the win, the Packers stayed undefeated and improved to their first 4–0 start since 1998.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-undefeatedsince98-21) ### Week 5: vs. Chicago Bears \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=16 "Edit section: Week 5: vs. Chicago Bears")\] Coming off a record-setting divisional road game against the Vikings, the Packers went home for a Sunday night divisional clash with their nemesis, the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears"). This would be the 174th meeting between the two teams. In the first quarter, Green Bay got off to a fast start by capping off the game's opening drive with rookie RB [DeShawn Wynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeShawn_Wynn "DeShawn Wynn") getting a 2-yard TD run for the only score of the period. In the second quarter, the Bears tied the game with RB [Cedric Benson's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_Benson "Cedric Benson") 10-yard TD run. The Packers would end the first half with QB [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") completing a 41-yard TD pass to WR [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings"), along with rookie kicker [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") converting a 37-yard field goal. In the third quarter, Chicago crept closer with kicker [Robbie Gould](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Gould "Robbie Gould") converting a 44-yard field goal. Green Bay responded with Crosby kicking a 37-yard field goal, yet the Bears pulled to within three as QB [Brian Griese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Griese "Brian Griese") completed a 19-yard TD pass to TE [Greg Olsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Olsen_/(American_football/) "Greg Olsen (American football)"). In the fourth quarter, Chicago erased their deficit completely with Gould's 36-yard field goal and Griese's 34-yard TD pass to TE [Desmond Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desmond_Clark "Desmond Clark"). With a turnover-plagued loss (5 turnovers on the night), the Packers fell to 4–1. Also, with two interceptions, Favre tied QB [George Blanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Blanda "George Blanda") at 277 for the most career interceptions.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-22) Also of note, [Brady Poppinga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brady_Poppinga "Brady Poppinga") intercepted a pass in the fourth quarter, extending the streak of at least one Packer interception per game for the 11th consecutive game. This matched the longest streak in team history, which occurred during an 11-game stretch in 1984–1985.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-calhoun2-23) * section: Week 6: vs. Washington Redskins")\] On October 14, 2007 [Charles Woodson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Woodson "Charles Woodson") picked up a [Santana in the game, his first of the season. This was the 12 straight game that Green Bay has recorded an interception, making it a new team record surpassing an 11-game stretch in 1984–1985.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-calhoun2-23)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-25) In the third quarter, Redskins safety [Sean Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Taylor "Sean Taylor") intercepted a Brett Favre pass making Favre the career interception leader in NFL history, eclipsing George Blanda's record of 277 interceptions. Favre threw two interceptions for the game.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-26) Woodson was named the NFC's Defensive Player of the Week for his performance versus the Redskins. It was the first time he has received this award.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-27) With the win, the Packers entered its bye week at 5–1. ### Week 8: at Denver Broncos \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=18 "Edit section: Week 8: at Denver Broncos")\] Following their bye week, the Packers flew to Denver to take on the Broncos on [Monday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monday_Night_Football "Monday Night Football"). In the first quarter, Bronco quarterback [Jay Cutler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Cutler "Jay Cutler") opened the scoring with a 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end [Tony Scheffler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Scheffler "Tony Scheffler"). On the first play of the ensuing series [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") completed a 79-yard touchdown to rookie wide receiver [James Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Jones_/(wide_receiver/) "James Jones (wide receiver)"). In the second quarter, rookie kicker [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") converted a 19-yard field goal, followed by a 26-yard field goal, and the Packers took a 13–7 lead into halftime. In the third quarter, Broncos kicker [Jason Elam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Elam "Jason Elam") converted a 45-yard field goal to cut Green Bay's lead to 3 points. In the fourth quarter, after getting the ball back with 2:27 remaining in the game, Cutler led a drive that began on the Bronco seven-yard line down the length of the field to the Green Bay four-yard line. On a 3rd and 1 Cutler attempted a quarterback draw to win the game, but [Ryan Pickett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Pickett "Ryan Pickett") stopped Cutler for no gain on the play. With no time outs remaining Elam and the kicking unit ran onto the field and converted a field goal to tie the game on the final play of the quarter. [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings") called heads and won the overtime coin toss, allowing Green Bay to receive the ball to begin overtime. On the first play, Favre threw an 82-yard touchdown pass to Jennings, who had outrun Bronco cornerback [Dré Bly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr%C3%A9_Bly "Dré Bly") for the catch. This was Favre's 13th TD pass of 75 yards or more, most of any player in NFL history.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-packers.com-28) Favre also becomes the first Packers player to throw two touchdown passes of 75 yards or more in the same game. Only three quarterbacks have accomplished the feat since 1990.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-packers.com-28) [Ryan Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Grant_/(running_back/) "Ryan Grant (running back)") ran for 104 yards, the first Packer to break the 100 yard rushing mark this season. With the win (their first ever in Denver), the Packers improved to 6–1. On November 1, 2007 [Aaron Kampman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Kampman "Aaron Kampman") was named the NFC Defensive Player of the Month for October, having recorded 5.5 sacks during that time period.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-29) Brett Favre was voted the Fedex Air and Ground NFL Player of the Week award for games played on October 28 – 29, the third time this season he has received this award.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-30) Wide receiver James Jones of the Packers was announced as the Diet Pepsi 2007 Rookie of the Week for games played on October 28–29. Jones made three receptions for 107 yards including a first-quarter 79-yard touchdown.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-31) ### Week 9: at Kansas City Chiefs \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=19 "Edit section: Week 9: at Kansas City Chiefs")\] Coming off their Monday Night road win over the Broncos, the Packers flew to [Arrowhead Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrowhead_Stadium "Arrowhead Stadium") for a Week 9 interconference duel with the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs"). After a scoreless first quarter, Green Bay drew first blood with rookie kicker [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") getting a 48-yard and a 36-yard field goal. However, the Chiefs would take the lead into halftime as RB [Larry Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Johnson_/(running_back/) "Larry Johnson (running back)") completed a 1-yard TD run. In the third quarter, the Packers regained the lead as Favre completed a 13-yard TD pass to WR [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings") for the only score of the period. In the fourth quarter, Kansas City regained the lead with QB [Damon Huard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damon_Huard "Damon Huard") completing a 30-yard TD pass to Johnson. Green Bay replied with Crosby kicking a 32-yard field goal, yet the Chiefs answered with Huard completing a 17-yard TD pass to TE [Tony Gonzalez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Gonzalez "Tony Gonzalez") (with RB [Priest Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priest_Holmes "Priest Holmes") getting the 2-point conversion run). The Packers pulled back into the lead as Favre and Jennings hooked up again on a 60-yard TD pass. Afterwards, Crosby made a 45-yard field goal, and CB [Charles Woodson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Woodson "Charles Woodson") returned an interception 46 yards for a touchdown. With the win, the Packers improved to 7–1. Brett Favre also became the third quarterback to defeat all of the other 31 NFL teams at least once. [Peyton Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peyton_Manning "Peyton Manning") and [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady") had been the first two to do so, just hours apart, the week before. The Packers scored 17 points in the final 3:05 on a defense that hadn't given up more than 20 all year.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-nfl.com-32) Favre joined [Peyton Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peyton_Manning "Peyton Manning") and [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady") as quarterbacks who've beaten all 31 other teams in the NFL.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-nfl.com-32) Favre rallied the Packers to victory from a fourth-quarter deficit or tie for the fourth time this season and 40th in his career, second only to John Elway's 46 fourth-quarter comebacks.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-33) The Packers have won 11 of their last 12 games, dating back to last season. Their sixth straight road wins tie for the second-longest away-from-home streak in team history.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-34) ### Week 10: vs. Minnesota Vikings \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=20 "Edit section: Week 10: vs. Minnesota Vikings")\] Playing their first home game since mid-October, the Packers hosted their division rivals, the [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings "Minnesota Vikings"). In the first half, the first career touchdown[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-35) by [Ryan Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Grant_/(running_back/) "Ryan Grant (running back)") came on a 30-yard run and gave the Packers a 7–0 lead, and two field goals by Mason Crosby (a 39-yard field goal midway through the 2nd quarter and a 24-yard field goal at the end of the half) would provide all the first half scoring, as the Packers went to the locker room leading 13–0. In the second half, Brett Favre threw a pair of third-quarter touchdown passes, one to Donald Lee and one to Ruvell Martin (which was Favre's 200th TD pass at Lambeau Field),[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-sportinglife.com-36) giving the Packers a 27–0 lead. With an additional Martin touchdown catch in the 4th quarter, the Packers shut out the Vikings 34–0, their first shutout of 2007. The Packers defense held [Adrian Peterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrian_Peterson "Adrian Peterson") to a season-low 45 yards on 11 carries a week after he set the NFL single-game rushing record with 296 yards against the San Diego Chargers.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-37) Grant became the first running back to reach the century mark against the Vikings this season, rushing for 119 yards on 25 carries, his career best.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-sportinglife.com-36) With the win, the Packers improved to 8–1, which matched the best start to a season in Brett Favre's career (in 1996 and 2002).[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-sportinglife.com-36) This game was the first time the Vikings had been shut out since 1991,[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-38) and halted the Vikings’ NFL-record run of 260 consecutive regular-season games with a point.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-39) The game was Green Bay's first shutout of the Vikings in 94 games of the rivalry.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-40) During the game, Favre became only the second NFL quarterback to throw for 60,000 yards in a career. He now has 60,257 yards' passing in his 17-year NFL career, second only to Dan Marino's career passing record of 61,361 yards.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-41) On November 15, 2007, the NFL announced Favre and running back Ryan Grant were voted the FedEx Air & Ground NFL Players of the Week for games played on November 11–12.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-42) Favre has received the FedEx Air award four times this season. Coach McCarthy was voted the Motorola NFL Coach of the Week for games played on November 11–12, the second time he has received the award this season.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-43) ### Week 11: vs. Carolina Panthers \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=21 "Edit section: Week 11: vs. Carolina Panthers")\] 38-year-old Brett Favre faced off against 44-year-old Carolina quarterback [Vinny Testaverde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinny_Testaverde "Vinny Testaverde") in a game that featured the oldest starting quarterbacks duo in NFL history.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-sports.yahoo.com-44) Favre threw 3 touchdown passes, and [Tramon Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tramon_Williams "Tramon Williams") returned a punt 94-yard for another touchdown as Green Bay defeated the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") 31–17. It was Favre's 62nd career game with at least three touchdown passes, tying [Dan Marino's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino") record. The win moved Green Bay to 9–1 on the season, its best start through the first 10 games since 1962.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-sports.yahoo.com-44) This is also Favre's best 10 game start to a season in his career.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-45) Packers punt returner Tramon Williams was named Special Teams Players of the Week for games played the 11th week of the 2007 season (November 18–19).[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-46) Packers defensive tackle [Corey Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Williams_/(American_football/) "Corey Williams (American football)") was voted the GMC Defensive Player of the Week for games played on November 18–19. Williams posted four solo tackles, two sacks and two forced fumbles during the game.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-47) ### Week 12: at Detroit Lions \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=22 "Edit section: Week 12: at Detroit Lions")\] Coming off their home win over the Panthers, the Packers flew to [Ford Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Field "Ford Field") for a Week 12 Thanksgiving NFC North duel with the [Detroit Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Lions "Detroit Lions"). Lions kicker [Jason Hanson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Hanson "Jason Hanson") completed a 47-yard field goal, and followed it with a 41-yarder to give the Lions a 6–0 lead after the first quarter. [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") started the second quarter with an 11-yard TD pass to [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings"). The Packers held on to the lead for the remainder of the game, winning 37–26. The win moved the Packers to 10–1 on the season. Favre finished the game with 3 touchdowns, the 63rd time he has thrown 3 or more touchdowns in a game, breaking the record he held with [Dan Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino"). At one point during the game, Favre completed 20 consecutive passes, breaking the Packers team record of 18 (held by [Don Majkowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Majkowski "Don Majkowski") and [Lynn Dickey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynn_Dickey "Lynn Dickey")).[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-48) Favre threw for 381 passing yards, which was his seventh 300-yard passing game of the season, tying a career-high.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-49) For his performance, Favre was awarded Fox's Galloping Gobbler Award. Favre also was voted Fedex Air NFL Player of the Week, the fifth time this year he has received the award.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-50) Green Bay has equaled its best 11-game record since 1929.[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-51) With the win, the Packers improved to 10–1 (the team's best start since 1962). * [![Image 23: A Detroit passing play](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Passing_Play.jpg/120px-Passing_Play.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Passing_Play.jpg "A Detroit passing play") A Detroit passing play * [![Image 24: Brett Favre kneels at the end of the game](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/70/DetroitLionsvsGreenBayPackers-2007-FavreKneel.jpg/120px-DetroitLionsvsGreenBayPackers-2007-FavreKneel.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DetroitLionsvsGreenBayPackers-2007-FavreKneel.jpg "Brett Favre kneels at the end of the game") ### Week 13: at Dallas Cowboys \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=23 "Edit section: Week 13: at Dallas Cowboys")\] Coming off their Thanksgiving win over their divisional foe, the Lions, the Packers flew to [Texas Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Stadium "Texas Stadium") for a Week 13 Thursday night intraconference duel with the throwback-clad [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys"). This match-up would see two 10–1 teams face one another for the first time since 1990 when the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants") lost to the [San Francisco 49ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers").[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-firstsince1990-52) Cowboys quarterback [Tony Romo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Romo "Tony Romo") faced off against his boyhood idol [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") in the game.[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-boyhoodidol-53) The Packers started the game missing two key players of their defense, with injured cornerback [Charles Woodson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Woodson "Charles Woodson") (tied for 7th in the NFL with 4 interceptions) and defensive end [Kabeer Gbaja-Biamila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabeer_Gbaja-Biamila "Kabeer Gbaja-Biamila") (tied for 6th in the NFL with 9.5 sacks) on the inactive list.[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-injuries-54) In the first quarter, Green Bay took the early lead as rookie kicker [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") completed a 47-yard field goal. On the second play of the Cowboys opening drive, Al Harris stripped the ball from Terrell Owens and side judge [Laird Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laird_Hayes "Laird Hayes") signaled Green Bay ball, but head linesman Derick Bowers overruled him. The only option for [Mike McCarthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_McCarthy "Mike McCarthy") to challenge on the play, since the whistle was blown, was whether it was a reception – the strip could not be reviewed. The replay upheld the reception and Dallas retained possession.[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-deadplay-55)[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-deadplay2-56)[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-deadplay3-57)[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-142penalty-58)[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-deadplay5-59) [Nick Folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Folk "Nick Folk") completed a 26-yard field goal to tie the game. Folk also completed a 51-yard field goal, and QB [Tony Romo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Romo "Tony Romo") threw a 3-yard TD pass to WR [Patrick Crayton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Crayton "Patrick Crayton"). The Packers would end the first quarter with rookie RB [Ryan Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Grant_/(running_back/) "Ryan Grant (running back)") running for a 62-yard touchdown. In the second quarter, Dallas responded with Romo completing a 26-yard TD pass to TE [Anthony Fasano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Fasano "Anthony Fasano") and a 10-yard TD pass to WR [Terrell Owens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrell_Owens "Terrell Owens"). [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") left the game in the second quarter after he hit his right elbow on the helmet of a blitzing Cowboys CB [Nate Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nate_Jones_/(cornerback/) "Nate Jones (cornerback)"). The throw led to Favre's second interception. Packers quarterback [Aaron Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers "Aaron Rodgers") took over for the Packers next series and led the offense on a 74-yard drive, capping it off with an 11-yard TD pass to WR [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings"). In the third, Grant finished off a 69-yard Packer drive with a 1-yard TD run for the only score of the quarter. In the fourth quarter, Romo completed a 4-yard TD pass to Crayton. Mason Crosby kicked a 52-yard field goal with just over 5 minutes remaining in the game to pull the Packers within a field goal. Dallas sealed the win as Folk kicked a 25-yard field goal with 1:03 left in the game. The Packers were flagged for a season-high 142 penalty yards.[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-142penalty-58) With the loss, the Packers fell to 10–2. This is the last Packers loss in Dallas to date, as the two teams would not meet again in Dallas until the [2013 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_season "2013 Green Bay Packers season"), where [Green Bay overcame a 26–3 deficit to beat the Cowboys 37–36](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers-Dallas_Cowboys_game "2013 Green Bay Packers-Dallas Cowboys game"). The Packers, since then, have gone 3–0-1 in Dallas in the regular season, the latest result being a 40–40 tie in [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Green_Bay_Packers_season "2025 Green Bay Packers season"). ### Week 14: vs. Oakland Raiders \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=24 "Edit section: Week 14: vs. Oakland Raiders")\] Hoping to rebound from their Thursday night road loss to the Cowboys, the Packers went home for Favre's 250th (270th including playoffs) consecutive start,[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-250starts-60) along with Green Bay's Week 14 interconference duel with the [Oakland Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Raiders "Oakland Raiders"). After a scoreless first quarter, the Packers sliced away in the second quarter with rookie RB [Ryan Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Grant_/(running_back/) "Ryan Grant (running back)") getting a 6-yard TD run, while CB [Will Blackmon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Blackmon "Will Blackmon") returned a punt 57 yards for a touchdown. The Raiders would end the half with their only score of the game as QB [Josh McCown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_McCown "Josh McCown") completed a 25-yard TD pass to WR [Jerry Porter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Porter_/(American_football/) "Jerry Porter (American football)"). In the third quarter, Green Bay took control with rookie [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") nailing a 44-yard field goal, QB [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") completing an 80-yard TD pass to WR [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings"), while Blackmon recovered an Oakland fumble in their endzone for a touchdown (making him the first player since Cincinnati's [Lemar Parrish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemar_Parrish "Lemar Parrish") in 1974 to return a punt and a fumble for a touchdown in one game). In the fourth quarter, the Packers pulled away with Favre completing a 46-yard TD pass to TE [Donald Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Lee_/(American_football/) "Donald Lee (American football)"). With the win, not only did Green Bay improve to 11–2, but they also clinched the NFC North division title.[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-divtitle-61) It was the Packers' 18th division title, along with their 24th playoff berth with three games remaining in the season – the second-fastest division title in team history.[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-fasttitle-62) Blackmon was awarded NFC Special Teams Player of the Week honors for his performance.[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-63) ### Week 15: at St. Louis Rams \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=25 "Edit section: Week 15: at St. Louis Rams")\] Coming off their dominating home win over the Raiders, the Packers flew to the [Edward Jones Dome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Jones_Dome "Edward Jones Dome") for a Week 15 duel with the [St. Louis Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Rams "St. Louis Rams"). In the first quarter, Green Bay drew first blood as rookie RB [Ryan Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Grant_/(running_back/) "Ryan Grant (running back)") got a 1-yard TD run. Afterwards, the Rams responded with QB [Marc Bulger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Bulger "Marc Bulger") completing a 4-yard TD pass to WR [Torry Holt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torry_Holt "Torry Holt"). In the second quarter, Green Bay went back into the lead as QB [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") completing a 4-yard TD pass to TE [Donald Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Lee_/(American_football/) "Donald Lee (American football)"), yet St. Louis answered with RB [Steven Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Jackson "Steven Jackson") getting a 46-yard TD run. The Packers would regain the lead prior to halftime with rookie kicker [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") getting a 44-yard field goal. In the third quarter, Green Bay took control as Crosby kicked a 50-yard field goal, along with Favre completing a 44-yard TD pass to WR [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings"). In the fourth quarter, the Pack finished the Rams off with Crosby nailing a 25-yard and a 46-yard field goal. With the win, the Packers improved to 12–2. Brett Favre came into the contest needing 184 yards to break [Dan Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino")'s all-time record mark of 61,361 career passing yards. He broke the record, as he threw for 227 total yards in the game. The new record came on a seven-yard completion to [Donald Driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Driver "Donald Driver"). [Ryan Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Grant_/(running_back/) "Ryan Grant (running back)") and [Greg Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Jennings "Greg Jennings") each had a touchdown during the game, making it the first time two Packers players have each scored a touchdown in the same four consecutive games.[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-4consecutivetds-64) [Atari Bigby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atari_Bigby "Atari Bigby") was voted the GMC Defensive Player of the Week for games played on December 13 – 17. Bigby made four tackles and two interceptions (a career high). Bigby intercepted the ball on the Packers' 22-yard line late in the second quarter to keep the Packers ahead by three going into halftime.[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-defpow-65) Kicker Mason Crosby was voted the Diet Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week for games played on December 13 – 17. Crosby went four-for-four in field goals, including a long 50-yard field goal and 46-yard and 44-yard kicks, and 3 for 3 in extra points.[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-masonrookie-66) With the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") defeating the [Seattle Seahawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Seahawks "Seattle Seahawks") on the day, the Packers clinched a first round bye for the playoffs. ### Week 16: at Chicago Bears \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=26 "Edit section: Week 16: at Chicago Bears")\] In cold and windy conditions, [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") threw 2 interceptions, and the Bears blocked 2 punts, en route to a 35–7 victory over the Packers, giving the Bears a sweep against Green Bay for the 2007 season. The Packers had not had a punt blocked in 12 years (929 punts).[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-929punts-67) The last time the Packers had 2 punts blocked in a game was September 21, 1975, in a game against Detroit.[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-2punts-68) Favre ended the game with 158 passing yards, and he surpassed 4,000 yards passing for the season, the 5th time in his career to achieve the mark. [Ryan Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Grant_/(running_back/) "Ryan Grant (running back)") ran for 100 total yards and the only touchdown for the Packers. With the loss, the Packers fell to 12–3 on the season. ### Week 17: vs. Detroit Lions \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season&action=edit§ion=27 "Edit section: Week 17: vs. Detroit Lions")\] [Brett Favre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre "Brett Favre") left less than a minute into the second quarter with the game well in hand, as he had thrown two touchdown passes, and running back [Ryan Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Grant_/(running_back/) "Ryan Grant (running back)") had another one on a 27-yard run. Backup quarterback [Craig Nall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Nall "Craig Nall") threw another touchdown in his first playing time in the NFL since 2004. Packers punter [Jon Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Ryan "Jon Ryan") had a 72-yard punt in the fourth quarter, the longest punt at Lambeau Field since 1965.[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-13wins-69) Running back [Brandon Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jackson_/(running_back/) "Brandon Jackson (running back)") topped the 100 yard mark for the first time in his career, running for 113 yards.[\[70\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-113yards-70) Packers rookie kicker [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") finished the season leading the NFL with 141 points, the highest-scoring season by a kicker in franchise history and third-highest season point total by any Packers player.[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-highestscoring-71) Green Bay has 17 consecutive home victories over Detroit, a team that has not recorded a victory in Wisconsin since 1991.[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-17consecutive-72) With their 5th straight win over the [Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Lions "Detroit Lions"), the Packers finished the season with a record of 13–3. The 13-win season was the fourth in the history of the Packer team (1997, 1996, and 1962 were the others).[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Green_Bay_Packers_season#cite_note-13wins-69) On January 2, 2008, Brandon Jackson was voted NFL Rookie of the Week for games played December 29–30, 2007.
